title: Define settlement correction, reversal uniqueness, and control-account projections
description:
References: §§5.6/5.7, 8.1/8.2, Appendix A/B/F (lines 419-423, 519-522, 536, 1165, 1241-1246, 1335, 1339).
Open amount = original minus summed SETTLES, but no immutable application-undo law is specified when a receipt or invoice is reversed/replaced. Reversing a settled receipt's GL legs leaves the invoice closed unless settlement effects reverse too; copying the original settles into the reversal can double-apply. Define versioned application effects and their bitemporal fold, target-side/unit validation, and over-application protection.
Acyclic SUPERSEDES plus exact target negation does not prevent two different idempotency keys from reversing/replacing one original twice. O + (-O) + (-O) is still acyclic and each reversal satisfies the local rule. Specify which reversal/replacement lifecycle actions are permitted and the concurrency witness; reversing a reversal must remain explicit if supported.
§5.6 says native detail postings inherently fold into the control account. The Register key schema has one account_ref, while only Leaf accounts accept legs. Define summary roll-up ownership, prohibit double counting and specify the externally fed detail-vs-summary representation so there is no second posting universe.
Acceptance: receipt applied then reversed; invoice replaced after partial application; concurrent duplicate reversals; two customers under an AR control account plus external-summary import. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.7 application effects versioned (open = original - SETTLES + UNSETTLES; reversals carry kernel-emitted unsettles; replacements re-declare, never copy); §8.2 reversal/replacement uniqueness by identity-derived vids (second reversal = AlreadyLive conflict; reversing a reversal explicit); §5.6 leaf-only register cells with rollup cells for summaries and external detail outside the book. FA-INV-08 clauses unsettle, reversed-once. Left open for re-review.

title: Remove the ungated full-byte document read (`Book::read_document`) that bypasses the privileged-caveat gate
description:
WHY: plan §9.6 interim posture: "privileged document bytes are stored in a separate PrivilegedDocument vertex class whose reads require the privileged caveat, evaluated by Steward before query construction — never as a result filter." fa-txf part C2 (88f4d46) implemented a gated `Book::read_document_for(capability, oid)` (crates/fa/src/book.rs:958) that derives redacted views, but the facade also exposes `pub fn read_document(&self, oid)` (book.rs:982) which calls `fa_journal::fetch_document` (crates/fa-journal/src/evidence.rs:783) with no capability and returns the full canonical bytes of any document, privileged or not. Any embedding caller (and any future surface wired to it) bypasses the redaction contract.

WHAT: make the ungated path unreachable from the facade: either remove `read_document` (callers migrate to `read_document_for` with the embedded-owner capability, which must hold `privileged` to see privileged bytes) or make it `pub(crate)` for verification-only internals with a doc comment stating why; audit every caller of `fetch_document` (`rg -n fetch_document crates`) so each sits behind an admission check or is a verify-only path that never returns bytes to a caller; add a topology/grep gate in check.sh that fails if a public facade fn returns `Document` bytes without a `Capability` parameter.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: owner posture with `privileged` reads full bytes via read_document_for; [ ] planted negative: a non-privileged capability receives only the redacted view; a compile-fail or gate test proves no public ungated byte path exists; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core for documents); [ ] consumers: fa-txf, fa-6l9 productions, fa-7dw; [ ] no-claim boundary: protects bytes at the facade; storage-level access to the book directory is outside this boundary (book keys).

TESTS: fa facade tests; fa-cli `document` binary tests; the gate's planted negative (a scratch fn added in a test fixture crate) logged.

title: fa-sim-harness: lab runtime (asupersync lab + substrate lab VFS) with registered crash points at every pipeline barrier, seeded scheduling, DPOR over post-vs-close and the other registered races, crashpacks with replay commands, in-sim consistency oracles; Genesis campaign green under lab (G1)
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): "Simulation-first (fa-sim)" is a design pillar (AGENTS.md verification ladder; plan §16) and Gate G1 requires the Genesis slice "green under lab and live". At 96d1918 there is no lab harness at all: no fa-sim-harness crate (W1 names it), no crash points, no DPOR, no crashpacks, no replay command; the only concurrency test is the policy-epoch race. The post-vs-close race that the doctrine calls "an SSI conflict, never a cron job's finding" is untested in either order. Every later workstream accrues its scenario campaigns onto this harness, so it is on the critical path to G1.

WHAT:
1. `crates/fa-sim-harness` (verification layer, test-only consumers): wraps asupersync's lab runtime (virtual time, seeded scheduling) and the substrate's lab VFS (torn writes, bit flips, ENOSPC, fsync lies) behind one `Lab { seed, schedule, vfs_faults }`; the facade `fa::Book` opens under it through the existing `Entropy::deterministic` and a lab `PurposeContexts` (no new API on Book that production code could reach).
2. Crash points at every pipeline barrier the kernel already has (admission, witnesses read, legs staged, mirrors moved, commit): a registered `CrashPoint` enum, each named in a `registries/crash_points.toml` row with the invariant it guards; the harness kills at each point and reopens; FA-INV-04/14/16 oracles (register-equals-fold, accumulator consistency, mirror-equals-payload) run after every reopen.
3. DPOR over post-vs-close, concurrent application, promotion-vs-trunk (when drafts exist), restatement-vs-reopen (when cases exist), sweep-vs-manual-void (fa-ctf): both orders explored; the winner is decided by first-committer-wins over witnesses, never by wall time.
4. Crashpacks: every failing seed writes `<scratch>/crashpacks/<seed>/` with the schedule, the VFS fault log and the exact `cargo test` replay command; the harness prints it; replay is byte-deterministic.
5. Consistency oracles as reusable in-sim checks: balance law, register-equals-fold, subledger-equals-control, admissibility at commit, SoD on approvals, idempotency stability, supersession acyclicity, accumulator consistency, bitemporal monotonicity, projection-equals-payload, erasure leaves amounts intact (those whose subsystems exist run; the rest are registered dormant with the activating bead).
6. Genesis campaign: the existing genesis/differential histories executed under the lab with 1,000 seeds and the full crash matrix; this is the G1 "green under lab" evidence.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `cargo test -p fa-sim-harness genesis_campaign` runs the matrix green and prints the seed count and crash-point coverage (every registered point hit ≥ 10 times); post-vs-close DPOR explores both orders and each ends in exactly one committed winner; [ ] planted negatives: a harness mutation that skips mirror moves on reopen fails register-equals-fold; a VFS torn-write at the commit barrier with the oracle disabled is caught by the accumulator-consistency check; [ ] proof class: bounded_model (the matrix states its bounds: seeds, depth, fault classes); [ ] consumers: Gate G1, every later campaign, fa-ctf interleavings, fa-s7x promotion races; [ ] no-claim boundary: a green campaign is bounded evidence, never a proof of crash safety beyond the registered points and seeds.

TESTS: the harness has its own unit tests for determinism (same seed → same transcript) and for crashpack replay; campaign logs record seed, point, oracle verdicts; run through rch like every other test.

title: Read-path authorization: every read verb takes a capability evaluated before query construction, with account/period/entity/known_at caveats and whole-entry visibility (doctrine 8, FA-INV-10.whole-entry)
description:
WHY: doctrine 8 — "Capability caveats are enforced before any storage observation … by refusal before query construction. Never as a result filter." At e606b46 balance/trial-balance/explain reads take no capability at all (crates/fa/src/book.rs:1162-1212); `entries_at`/`report_at` fold the whole book (crates/fa-registers/src/lib.rs:228-252, :910). The plan's Auditor (`known_at ≤ seq`), Regulator (scoped, time-boxed), and Production profiles, and the `accounts ⊆ subtree`, `periods`, `entities`, `dimensions` caveats are therefore unexpressible for reads. Separately, an Agent-profile capability is refused on document reads because the read is built with `trunk: true` and trips the trunk-write rule (crates/fa-journal/src/redaction.rs:548, crates/fa-policy/src/admit.rs:39) — reads and writes must be distinct admission classes.

WHAT:
1. fa-policy: `admit_read(capability, ReadScope { verb, coordinate, accounts?, periods?, entities? })` evaluated before any snapshot read; refusal FA-REF code naming the blocking caveat (catalog row); read admission never applies the trunk-write rule.
2. Facade/CLI/fad/MCP: every read verb (tb, explain balance, open-items, entry show, verify *, document read, checkpoint verify, registers materialize's read half) takes the session capability (fa-r3q) or the embedded-owner capability.
3. Whole-entry visibility (§14.2): an entry is observable iff every leg's account and dimensions are in scope; folds over in-scope accounts include in-scope legs of partially visible entries; `explain balance` marks `partially_visible` only under `partial_view`; certificates (fa-cqk) name the capability commitment; a partial fold is never labelled whole-book.
4. known_at caveat: an Auditor pinned `known_at ≤ s` cannot select a later coordinate (refusal), and historical selectors never resurrect revoked authority.
5. fa-reference: visibility model; differential on generated scopes.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] positive: an Auditor token pinned at seq s reads tb at s and is refused at head; an account-subtree token's tb contains only that subtree and its certificate names the scope;
[ ] planted negatives: a read whose scope excludes an account the request names → refused before any snapshot read (proven by a counting probe: zero substrate reads on refusal); a partially visible entry without partial_view is not listed; an Agent token reading a document succeeds (regression for the trunk-write misfire);
[ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.whole-entry live) + differential;
[ ] consumers: fa-7dw, fa-zgn (engagements), fa-9ae certificates, examiners;
[ ] no-claim boundary: authorization of reads is enforced in FrankenAccounting before query construction (R-WARDEN interim), not by substrate predicate compilation.

TESTS: fa-policy unit; fa-journal/fa-registers kernel tests with a substrate read counter; CLI binary tests per verb; differential with seeds logged.

comments.text:
## 2026-10-20 (StormyLion, claude-opus-5-5): slice 1 landed at main/master fa7eb191 (fa7eb191). Scoped read tokens on the core read verbs. Still open

**What landed:**
- **Kernel:**
  - `ReadAuthority::whole_book(seq)`.
  - `grant_refusal` now refuses a grant that drops the issuer's redaction caveat.
  - Scope caveats need no grant rule. Issuance is a whole-book act, so admission refuses any issuer carrying accounts, periods, effective, known-at or branch. A scoped token can never issue at all; this is now tested at the kernel and through the CLI.
- **Facade:** `ReadScope::admit_report(&ReportSelection, known_at)` and `admit_as_of(day, known_at)` judge a native report's reach at its recorded frontier before the query:
  - stock TB through its latest period;
  - activity and explain on exactly their periods;
  - open items on the whole book.

  The existing ReadScope readers share them.
- **CLI:** `tb` (plain and certified, with period, activity or as-of selections), `explain balance`, `open-items` (snapshot, plain and certified) and `entry show` admit the session capability with `read_scope` before the book is observed, then admit their selection. Out of scope is FA-REF-011, exit 7, naming the caveat, and is never a filtered answer.
- **Issuance:** `fa capability issue` gains `--period <code>`... (an unknown code is usage, exit 2), `--effective-through YYYY-MM-DD` and `--known-at-most <seq>`.
- **Display:** `capability show`/`list` render every scope caveat. The `issued_capability` shape gains books, accounts, periods, effective_through, known_at_most, branch and redaction, nullable and additive; the pin was regenerated.

**Acceptance status:**
- [x] Positive, through `fa --token`:
  - A March-only token reads March activity: the same rows as the owner, not a subset.
  - A token pinned at seq s reads at s (equal to the owner's read at s, unequal to the head) and is refused at the head.
  - An effective-through token reads stock through its day.
- [x] Planted negatives, out of scope are refused (FA-REF-011) before the query:
  - stock TB, as-of TB, another period's activity, a certified April TB, another period's explanation, open items, entry show.
  - A period-scoped issuer issues nothing (FA-REF-011, nothing journaled, no token file).
  - A redaction-confined issuer cannot drop its redaction caveat (kernel test).
- [ ] Zero substrate reads on refusal: needs a substrate read counter.
- [ ] Whole-entry visibility for `accounts` caveats: reads under one are still refused outright by `admit_reads`.
- [ ] The other read verbs: explain period/entry/register/lineage/evidence, event, verify, document read, export, triage.
- [ ] The fa-reference visibility model and its differential.
- [ ] An Agent token reading a document (the trunk-write misfire regression): not re-checked in this slice.

title: Robot envelope parity with Appendix D (v, coordinate, warnings, next_actions, refusal_id, certificate) with the robot-schema fixture pin, --yes/confirm_plan gating of dangerous verbs (exit 7), NO_COLOR/CI/TERM/non-TTY styling, fa triage/doctor/next/explain lineage, simulated-agent corpus with zero useless_error
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): The agent-ergonomics Polish Bar is a release gate (G3) and the robot envelope is the agent contract. At 96d1918 the envelope is event-discriminated NDJSON with sorted keys and the exit-code dictionary is enforced (tests in fa-cli/tests/cli.rs), but Appendix D fields `v`, `coordinate`, `warnings`, `next_actions`, `refusal_id` are absent (0 hits), `certificate` is always null (fa-intents bead), `--yes` and `--no-color` are parsed by fa-cli/src/args.rs but never read by any handler, there is no ANSI styling path at all, and `fa triage`, `fa doctor`, `fa next`, `fa explain` beyond `balance` do not exist (0 hits). The refusal constants also diverge from Appendix D's numbering (code's 004 = unknown account vs D's 004 = closed period; 013 agent-trunk vs pending-resolved) — that reconciliation is fa-coa's.

WHAT:
1. Envelope: add `v` (envelope minor), `coordinate { book, branch, known_at, effective }` on every data event, `warnings: []` (always present), `next_actions: []` (verbs the agent should run next, from a registry table in verbs.toml), `refusal_id` on every refusal (the catalog code) and `certificate` (from fa-intents); `fa robot-docs schema` prints them; a pinned fixture `registries/robot_schema/<minor>.jsonl` is compared byte-for-byte by a check.sh step (the "robot-schema fixture pin" named in AGENTS.md).
2. `--yes`: dangerous verbs (period close/lock/reopen, resolve voids, post under post_closed, registers materialize over existing, any erasure) refuse with exit 7 and name the safe alternative unless `--yes` or a matching `--confirm-plan` certificate is given; `fa capabilities --json` lists which verbs are dangerous.
3. Styling: a single `Style` resolved once from `NO_COLOR`, `CI`, `TERM=dumb`, non-TTY, `--no-color`; human mode uses it for tables; robot mode never styles; stderr-only diagnostics; `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` affects display fields only (test).
4. Mega-commands: `fa triage` (book health, daemon absent/present, periods, due holds, due reversals, drift, next_command), `fa doctor` (environment: toolchain, book dir, keys, daemon socket, registries embedded minor), `fa next` (the next admissible verb given the book state and the capability), `fa explain lineage <entry>` (plan §7.3 net effect).
5. Intent inference: Levenshtein-1 (the code is ≤ 2 today; tighten to the registry's rule and keep the test), alias set from verbs.toml, mis-ordered coordinate flags accepted; correction suggests but never executes a write verb.
6. Fresh-context simulated-agent corpus: a scripted agent (no model) runs every §15.6 workflow against the binary and asserts zero `useless_error` outcomes (every refusal carries a fix that works when followed).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: every data event carries v/coordinate/warnings/next_actions and the fixture pin is byte-identical; `fa period close --json` without `--yes` exits 7 naming `--dry-run`/`--yes`, with `--yes` proceeds; `NO_COLOR=1 fa tb` has no escape bytes; `fa triage` on a book with a due hold reports it with `next_command`; [ ] planted negatives: a handler that emits an event missing `coordinate` fails the schema test; a dangerous verb without the gate fails the dangerous-verb table test; [ ] proof class: gate (fixture pin) + regression tests; [ ] consumers: fa-mcp (same envelope), the Polish Bar G3 review, every agent; [ ] no-claim boundary: envelope parity proves the contract shape, not agent success rates (those come from the corpus).

TESTS: fa-cli binary tests per item with the captured stdout logged on failure; the simulated-agent corpus as an integration test with a per-workflow transcript.

title: Capability revocation surface: Book::revoke_capability, `fa capability revoke` (verbs.toml, robot event), MCP parity
description:
WHY: e97746b (fa-llx) journals revocation (fa_journal::revoke_capability, PolicyControl CapabilityEvent{Revoke}, FA-REF-023) and every Steward-checked write witnesses it (fa-bcd), but nothing above the kernel can revoke: the facade has no method, the CLI no verb, the MCP no tool. An operator who learns a token leaked has no way to revoke it short of linking fa-journal. Plan §14.2 (revocation is a journaled control), Appendix D (one verb registry for CLI/daemon/MCP).

WHAT: (1) facade Book::revoke_capability(capability, revoked_commitment, effective_date, idempotency_key, description) -> Outcome<Revoked> (mirrors Book::approve); (2) CLI `fa capability revoke --commitment <hex> --as <principal> [--grant issue_capability] --json` emitting a `capability_revoked` event {control_entry, recorded_at, already_recorded}; dangerous-op gating per fa-12x (--yes or plan) since revocation is irreversible; (3) a way to learn a capability's commitment (`fa capabilities --json` already prints capability fields: add commitment if absent); (4) verbs.toml rows + robot-schema re-pin + MCP parity row.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] CLI revoke then a post/transition/tick under the revoked token refuses FA-REF-023 exit 7 end-to-end; [ ] re-running the same revoke is already_recorded (idempotent) and writes nothing; [ ] a revoker without issue_capability is FA-REF-011; [ ] parity gate green; [ ] the refusal's fix for FA-REF-023 names the verb that issues a fresh capability.

Owners: facade + kernel call MistyPlateau; CLI verb, envelope and MCP JadePeak's lane.

(1) `--format toon` on every read verb; amounts stay strings; (2) encoder golden vectors from the TOON spec fixtures; (3) a differential test that round-trips through `tru` when it is installed (UNRUN otherwise); (4) robot-docs guide mentions when to prefer TOON. title: Key-file permissions are never checked (plan §15.3 exit 4) and fad.lease is created or truncated in any --book directory, following symlinks: check 0600/owner on every key load, take the lease only in a verified book directory, never for discovery commands, never through a symlink
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14 at 9e83c3f)
- **Key-file permissions are never checked.** `book.keys` is read with no mode check (crates/fa/src/book.rs:174-215). Plan §15.3 maps wrong permissions on the three-line DatabaseKeys file to exit 4 with a fix, and App H R-KEY says the 0600 key file is managed by fad.
- **The lease file is created anywhere.** `Lease::acquire` creates or truncates `<dir>/fad.lease` in whatever directory `--book`/`FA_BOOK` names (crates/fad/src/lease.rs:84-107). This happens even during discovery commands and in directories that are not books, and it follows symlinks.

## What to build
1. On every key load, refuse when the mode is wider than 0600 or the owner differs from the process uid. Exit 4, with a catalog code naming the path, the observed mode and `chmod 600 <path>` as the fix. `fa doctor` reports the same check.
2. Only acquire the lease inside a directory that passes the book-identity check, and never for discovery commands (help, version, capabilities, robot-docs).
3. Open the lease file with O_NOFOLLOW (or check `symlink_metadata` first, through asupersync's fs).
4. Create the lease file without truncating an existing non-lease file.

## Acceptance
Each failure case below has a planted test, and each one leaves the file system unchanged (compare hashes and mtimes):
- a key file at 0644 → exit 4;
- `--book` pointing at a non-book directory → no lease file created;
- a symlinked `fad.lease` → refused;
- `fa --help` with `FA_BOOK` set → no lease file created.

## Tests & logging
fa-cli and fad tests with tempdirs. Each case logs the path, the observed mode, the decision and the refusal id.

title: Certification must not invalidate plans: plans bind to the accounting frontier, not raw HEAD; a read-only session's --certify cannot break other principals' outstanding plans
description:
## The defect
An MCP session launched as Agent with only `read` can call fa_read_trial_balance with certify: true.
That retains a Certificate (Book::retain_certificate, book.rs ~1182, takes no capability) and advances
the book frontier, so every outstanding PostPlan then fails FA-REF-034 (plan.rs ~330: exact basis
sequence). A read-only principal can thus invalidate everyone's reviewed plans — and the Agent profile
is documented as never writing trunk.

## Design options (pick one, document the choice)
A (preferred): plans bind to the *accounting frontier* = the highest commit sequence that changed any
state a plan witnesses (entries, periods, policies, approvals, capabilities, limits, chart). Pure
metadata (certificates, access events, checkpoints) does not move it. Commit re-validates the plan's
witness set at the current snapshot exactly as today.
B: certification by Agent profiles writes to a session-local or draft store, never trunk.
Either way, retaining a certificate requires `read` + an explicit `certify` op (or `produce`).

## Tests
Agent certifies a TB between another principal's plan and commit → commit succeeds; an accounting change
in between → PlanInvalidated (FA-REF-034) as before; certification without the op is refused.
acceptance_criteria: The three scenarios behave as stated through the library, CLI and MCP.
close_reason: Bound PostPlan to accounting frontier via delta_since metadata classification and basis/birth-ordinal-independent effects_digest, enforced read capability on Book::retain_certificate_authorized, and verified across fa-journal, fa-cli, and fa-mcp e2e_stdio

Binding plans to an accounting frontier means: classify every commit in (basis, head] via delta_since as metadata-only (report certificates, access events, checkpoints) or accounting; re-prepare at head and compare effects_digest instead of basis; and re-anchor recorded_plan (the entry's created_at is no longer basis+1). Option B (Agent certification writes to a session/draft store) depends on drafts (fa-s7x). The owner's MCP e2e deliberately asserts that an Agent can certify, so "certify requires produce" was rejected. Needs a ruling between A and B before code.

title: fa-mcp containment: never accept `as`/`grant`/`yes`/`keys` from tool arguments; bind the server's principal and Agent-profile capability at launch; stop the self-approval detector coaching impersonation
description:
WHY: verified at e606b46 — fa-mcp turns agent-supplied tool arguments into fa argv including `--as <principal>`, `--grant <op>`, `--yes` and `--keys <path>` (crates/fa-mcp/src/registry.rs:1381-1388; global flags validated as exposed at :353; unit test :1775-1800 asserts `{"grant":"post_closed","yes":true}` becomes `--grant post_closed --yes`). Every fa-cli handler then self-issues a Human capability for that principal and those ops (`Capability::embedded`, crates/fa-policy/src/capability.rs:237-247). So the MCP surface — the surface built for AI agents — gives an agent full Human authority, lets it choose its identity per call (defeating segregation of duties: plan as `operator`, approve as `controller`), and lets it bypass dangerous-operation gating by passing `yes: true`. The self-approval detector (crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:478-492) answers a detected self-approval with "call fa_time_approve with `as` set to a different, admissible principal" plus a suggested tool call `{"as": "<another principal>"}`: the exact impersonation the plan's §14.3/§14.4 forbid. This is the cheapest high-value fix in the reality check and can land before the full issuance model (fa-v62/fa-r3q).

WHAT:
1. Server launch configuration (CLI args of the fa-mcp binary, never tool arguments): `--book <dir>`, `--keys <file>`, `--principal <name>`, `--profile agent|preparer` (default `agent`), optional `--grant <op>` list bounded by the profile (an Agent profile cannot hold approve/close/reopen/restate/post_closed/migrate/witness/issue_capability/erase). Until fa-v62 lands, the server self-issues exactly one capability at launch from this config and labels every response `authority: {posture: "mcp-launch-config", principal, profile, ops}`.
2. Tool schemas: remove `as`, `grant`, `yes`, `keys` and `book` overrides from every tool's input schema; the argument normalizer refuses them if present with a structured error `{type: "forbidden_argument", data: {fix_hint: "identity and authority are fixed when the server starts; ask the operator to start a server with the profile you need", argument}}` (never silently ignores them).
3. Dangerous operations through MCP require a `confirm_plan` certificate once fa-we7 lands; until then they are refused through MCP with the safe alternative (`--dry-run`/plan file for lock/reopen) — an agent never confirms its own dangerous op with `yes`.
4. Self-approval detector: the fix text names the policy row and says a second, independent approver (a human or a separately launched approver session holding approve) must approve; the suggested tool call is removed. Same audit for every other detector's fix text (`grep -n '"as"' crates/fa-mcp/src`).
5. verbs.toml `[mcp]` rows and the robot-schema pin updated; parity tests updated deliberately (show the before/after diff in the commit message).
6. `fa capabilities --json` and the MCP `robot_docs`/server instructions state the actual binding posture.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] positive: an fa-mcp e2e (stdio) session launched with `--profile agent --principal agent-7` can call read tools and `post` on a draft-less book and receives FA-REF-013 (Agent-on-trunk) with the drafts pointer — proving the Agent profile now reaches the kernel from a real surface;
[ ] planted negatives (each reaches exactly one check): a tool call carrying `as` → forbidden_argument; carrying `grant` → forbidden_argument; carrying `yes` → forbidden_argument; a server launched `--profile agent --grant approve` refuses to start with the profile-bound reason; the self-approval detector's output contains no `as` override and no suggested approve call;
[ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core reached from the MCP posture) + e2e;
[ ] consumers: every MCP host, fa-ohe, fa-z5u (fad-hosted MCP);
[ ] no-claim boundary: launch configuration is trusted operator input; this does not authenticate the operator (fa-v62/fa-r3q do).

TESTS: crates/fa-mcp/tests/e2e_stdio.rs cases above with the full JSON-RPC transcript logged on failure; registry.rs unit tests replacing the current `grant`/`yes` pass-through test (the old test is restated, not deleted: it becomes the negative); detect.rs unit test for the new self-approval text.
close_reason: Verified on main (6abaf42): fa-mcp principal/capability launch containment and self-approval guidance landed and tested in crates/fa-mcp/tests/mcp.rs.

title: Kernel settlement ignores the legal-entity dimension: a receipt for entity A can settle entity B's invoice on the same account

The kernel's settlement admission compares account, unit and side but not the leg's dimensions
(crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:1419-1434). `fa/src/settlement.rs` enforces "same dimensions" only at the
surface layer, so any library or future surface that bypasses it violates per-entity balance semantics
(§4.1, §5.2, §5.7). Also confirm the reference oracle's settlement model includes the entity.

## What to build

naming both entities. Oracle mirrors it independently.

## Acceptance

differential over generated multi-entity histories green.

title: Teller reconciliation: bank statement parsers to BankLine documents with import receipts, matching engine as adaptive decisions with decision cards and a deterministic pinned fallback, journaled Match objects with exact residual explanations, reconciliation register verified by fold with RegisterEquals attestations, three-way matching, fa bank import / fa reconcile
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Teller is bank reconciliation: bank statement parsers producing BankLine documents (W4), a matching engine whose heuristics are adaptive decisions with decision cards and a deterministic pinned fallback (AGENTS.md adaptive-decision contract), a reconciliation register and attestations. At 96d1918 there is no Teller code (2 prose hits). fa-ff6 (bank feeds through flywheel_connectors) presumes BankLine documents and the matching engine, so it depends on this bead. Reconciliation is also one of Lantern's procedures and one of the registers the plan verifies by fold.

WHAT:
1. Bank statement parsers in `fa-formats` (interop) for CSV/OFX/CAMT.053 subsets, exact amounts (fa-money), every line a content-addressed `BankLine` document (Docket) with the statement's import receipt (Docket slice 2) and `DERIVED_FROM` the statement document; fuzzed readers.
2. `crates/fa-teller` (analytics): candidate generation (amount, date window, counterparty normalization, reference tokens), scoring as an adaptive decision: the decision card records the policy epoch, state space, candidates, observed features, the expected-benefit interval and the pinned fallback (exact amount + date within N days + reference equality, deterministic tie-break by lowest entry ordinal); learned scores are advisory features only; the card never changes a committed amount.
3. Match decisions as journaled, immutable objects (`Match { bank_line_ref, entry_ref | None, decision_card_ref, principal }`), one-to-many and many-to-one with exact residual explanations (fees, FX) that must be posted as their own entries under a named law, never absorbed; unmatching is a new object with lineage.
4. The reconciliation register: per bank account × period, book balance vs statement balance with the outstanding items list as a fold of matches and bank lines; `fa verify reconciliation` refolds it; reconciliation attestations bind `cell_key + fold_digest` (RegisterEquals).
5. Three-way matching (PO/receipt/invoice) as the same engine over documents, registered as a Lantern procedure.
6. CLI: `fa bank import <file> --account <code> --json`, `fa reconcile <account> --for <period> [--dry-run] --json` (plans the matches as intents with certificates; `--yes` or confirm_plan to commit), `fa reconcile status`.

title: Findings as journaled, certified objects (plan §11.8): Finding with CITES edges and run certificate, FindingReview control life cycle (acknowledge/dismiss with reason/escalate, SoD), numbered Workpapers, `fa finding list|show|review|export` + MCP — Lantern findings are in-memory structs today
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-10-14)
Plan §11.8 and §11.1 require findings to be **registered, certified, bit-reproducible, immutable journal objects**:
- `CITES` edges to the legs, entries, documents and BankLines they rest on;
- review and dismissal as control effects with lineage, never as edits;
- workpapers numbered `FA-<book>-WP-<seq>`;
- `fa finding export --format md|jsonl`.

The investigator workflow of §15.6 ends with exactly these steps: `fa finding export` and `fa access log`.

Today, Lantern (integration line only) returns findings as in-memory structs (fa-lantern lib.rs:16-20 says so). Nothing is journaled, so a finding cannot be cited, reviewed, dismissed, replayed or produced. No bead owned this; fa-nlu and fa-ac78 cover procedures, not the finding object.

## What to build
1. **The Finding object.** Fields:
   - procedure id, version and registry row digest;
   - parameters digest and coordinate (known-at, effective, branch);
   - claim class (statistical / invariant per the registry; exact procedures such as tracing and aging get their own deterministic class, not "statistical");
   - severity, narrative template id;
   - cited object refs, and the run certificate.

   It is written by a `RecordFindings` intent inside one transaction per run. The writes are idempotent by the derived identity (procedure, parameters, coordinate).
2. **Review life cycle.** `FindingReview` control entries: Acknowledged, Dismissed (with a reason code and evidence), Escalated. SoD: a reviewer may not be the principal who ran the procedure, if the registry says so.
3. **Workpapers.** A `Workpaper` object groups findings and certificates under a sequential per-book number, assigned at commit, not by the caller.
4. **Surfaces.** `fa finding list|show|review|export` and the MCP tools, with verbs.toml rows (fa-mg2j ops: read / review / produce).
5. **Verification.** `fa replay` of a run certificate re-derives the same Finding set, byte-identical.

## Acceptance
- A run over the 30-entry Lantern corpus journals its findings. Replay reproduces them. A second identical run is a no-op that returns the same ids.
- Dismissal requires a reason. Self-review is refused per the SoD row.
- The workpaper export is deterministic (same bytes twice), and every citation resolves.
- FA-INV-11 has a clause covering findings (fa-j6ue) and it is live.

## Tests & logging
- Binary e2e (`fa` and `fa-mcp` stdio) and a lab crash test between run and commit (all-or-nothing).
- Each test logs the procedure, the finding ids, the citations count and the certificate oid.
close_reason: Promoted FA-INV-11.finding-replay to live with shipped_capabilities.finding mapping; added 30-entry Lantern corpus finding/workpaper/retry test and lab FaultVfs crash test in crates/fa/src/findings/tests.rs; verified 43/43 fa findings tests and 9/9 fa-registry invariant tests.

The FX kernel is live but nothing reaches it.
- **What is live:**
  - post.rs admits valued entries: `fx::admit_structure`, then recomputation against witnessed Rate documents inside the posting transaction (fa-s3c).
  - fa-journal has the planners: `value_proposal` (SpotClose / PeriodAverage), `plan_revaluation` (PeriodEndRevaluation), `plan_realized_fx_settlement`.
  - fa-registers folds functional currency and refuses unvalued foreign legs.
- **What is missing:** no facade wrapper, CLI verb, intent field or MCP tool names any of it.
  - A `fa post` intent cannot carry base_amount or base_totals (fa-cli never parses them).
  - There is no way to add a Rate document: FxRateDocument is a binary canonical encoding (magic, version, units, reduced rate, rounding, as_of, retrieved_at, purpose, source), and `fa document add` takes host bytes.
  - `fa verify fx-conversion`, named in fa-s3c's title, does not exist (verify has registers, open-items, availability, usage, accumulator, projections, schedules, periods, replay, close).
  - So a multi-currency book posts per-unit-balanced entries with no functional-currency valuation, and the functional fold refuses them.

## Owner decisions first (doctrine: "Do not convert currencies with a rate you typed. Rates are documents")
1. **Rate-document intake.** Which sources may create a Rate document?
   - Options: a provider file reader (ECB/central-bank XML, CSV), with source and retrieval proof; a typed rate under an explicit grade (HumanUpload vs AgentUpload) and the evidence minimum for kind Rate (evidence_policy.toml kind 3); or both.
   - The answer fixes the CLI shape (`fa fx rate import|add`) and whether agents may create rates at all.
2. **Valuation at posting.** Who calls `value_proposal`?
   - Options: the intent names `fx: {law, rates: [D:oid…]}` and the CLI values it before the kernel's own recomputation; or the typed verbs (fa-i7e) do it.
3. **Revaluation and realized FX.** `fa revalue` (fa-i7e) vs a close task (fa-4o0). The functional balance and carrying basis come from the fa-registers functional fold.

## Then build (each with a verbs.toml row, MCP tool, pin, and a real-binary test with planted negatives)
- Rate-document intake per decision 1.
- Valued posting per decision 2.
  - Positive: an EUR sale valued at a SpotClose rate posts with base_totals citing the rate document; the functional TB balances.
  - Negatives: a missing rate document, wrong purpose, as_of ≠ effective date, a tampered base_amount.
- `fa revalue` and `fa verify fx-conversion`.
- A functional-currency trial balance view, if not already reachable.

## Related
- fa-s3c (closed): FX posting kernel; its title names `fa verify fx-conversion`, which no surface provides.
- fa-i7e: typed verbs, including `revalue`; decision 3 decides whether revaluation lives there.
- fa-z41: the 2026-10-11 epic of vision goals with no bead coverage ("FX posting").
- No dependency edges were added at filing: a swarm was active, and graph structure has one writer.

title: fa-cli: canonicalize --book / FA_BOOK before any substrate path use (a '..' component reaches fgdb-strata's and the blob store's rename, which the host VFS refuses) — planted '..' negative, byte-identical envelope for the absolute and relative spellings
description: WHY (TopazOsprey 3656, 2026-10-11, unverified observation during fa-txf t8): fa-cli's book_dir passes --book / FA_BOOK through raw. asupersync's UnixVfs::rename runs validate_safe_path (fs/path_ops.rs ~189), which refuses any '..' component, while create_dir_all and open do not validate; so a book opened as --book ../acme most likely fails at the substrate's first staging rename (fgdb-strata store.rs ~1014) or the blob store's rename, with an I/O error instead of a usable book. Agents are the primary operators and relative spellings are what they type. WHAT: (1) resolve the book directory once at the CLI boundary (fa-cli book_dir): join to the process cwd and normalize '.' and '..' lexically (no symlink resolution, no host canonicalize of a path that may not exist yet), refuse a path that escapes nothing but still carries '..' only if the normalized form cannot be produced; pass the normalized absolute path to Book::open and to the daemon request (through_daemon already prefers files.cwd); (2) the same normalization in fad's request handling so a daemon-side open sees the same path; (3) first verify the failure with a binary test (fa book create --book ../x from a temp cwd) and keep that test as the planted negative turned positive. ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: --book ../acme, --book ./acme and --book /abs/acme produce byte-identical robot envelopes (coordinate.book, data) for the same book; [ ] planted negative: before the fix the '..' spelling fails at the substrate rename (recorded in the test's doc as the observed defect), after the fix no substrate call ever sees a '..' component (a FaultVfs or path-recording VFS asserts it); [ ] proof class: invariant (one normalization point) + binary test; [ ] consumers: every agent invocation of fa with a relative --book, fad clients, the MCP posture (fa-mcp forwards cwd); [ ] no-claim boundary: this does not make the substrate tolerate '..'; it keeps such paths out of it.
close_reason: Verified on main (6abaf42): fa-cli canonicalizes --book / FA_BOOK before substrate path use with planted '..' negative and byte-identical envelope tests in crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs.

title: Close engine: CloseRun/CloseTask DAG, incremental YearEndClose (Closing class) under the chart's closes_to map, FA-INV-03.nominal-zero, `fa close dry-run|run|status`, `fa verify close`, reclose deltas, rehearsal on a scratch book
description:
WHY: plan §7.5 "The close as a graph" — a CloseRun is a control object for (book, period) with CloseTask vertices and DEPENDS_ON edges (reconcile, accrue, depreciate, revalue, allocate, intercompany, eliminate, roll forward, produce statements, attest, lock); "every close is first rehearsed on a branch"; year-end Closing-class entries are real, incremental (each run closes the not-yet-closed net of every nominal account to closes_to — retained earnings, AOCI, fund balance), and FA-INV-03 `nominal-zero` requires Σ nominal balances for the year = 0 after the latest Closing entry (`fa verify close FY2026`). §15.6's first worked workflow ("The agent closes a month") and the README (`fa close dry-run --period 2026-03 --draft close-2026-03`) depend on it. At e606b46: the Closing class is refused FA-REF-102 (crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:259); CloseRun exists only as a symbol id; `closes_to` is not on AccountRow; nominal-zero is dormant (registries/invariants.toml); no close verb exists. No bead covers the close engine (fa-xwv specifies stock/flow fold semantics; fa-9ae mentions closing identities only as test expectations).

WHAT: (1) chart: `closes_to` on Account (or a per-chart map) as a journaled schema effect; nominal account types per registries/account_types.toml. (2) Closing class admitted per Appendix C (W(close) in Open/SoftClosed, W(close,1) in Closed, W(restate,2) inside an Approved case in Locked) with the incremental law: closing legs = − (fold of nominal legs effective in FY − prior Closing legs) per account/unit/entity, to closes_to; zero-delta reclose emits nothing; income-statement folds carry exclude_classes [Closing] (fa-xwv). (3) CloseRun lifecycle object (Appendix A) with CloseTask vertices and a task registry (registries/close_tasks.toml: id, depends_on, the procedure/rule/intent it runs, evidence requirement, approver role) — tasks that need unbuilt subsystems (revalue, eliminate, statements) are registered with status unsupported(bead) and the run refuses to mark them done, never skips them silently. (4) `fa close dry-run --period P` replays trunk into a scratch book (Book::replay_into_scratch exists, crates/fa-journal/src/scratch.rs) and executes every supported automated task there, reporting the resulting tb diff vs trunk and per-task outcomes with a certificate (fa-cqk); `fa close run` executes on trunk task by task (each task obtains a fresh basis, plan §5.10) under the close capability; `fa close status`. (5) `fa verify close <FY>`: nominal-zero at the known-at of the latest Closing entry, exit 8 otherwise. (6) fa-reference: naive incremental close + nominal-zero oracle; differential including post-close adjustments and reclose.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: FY with revenue/expense legs → close → nominal accounts fold to zero, retained earnings equals net income; an audit adjustment after close → reclose emits only the delta; dry-run on scratch leaves trunk's journal head unchanged; [ ] planted negatives: Closing posted by a principal without close → refused; a task depending on an unfinished task → run refuses; a hand-made Closing entry that does not zero nominals → `fa verify close` exit 8; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-03.nominal-zero live) + differential; [ ] consumers: §15.6 workflow, fa-9ae statements, fa-y4v, AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED (first Lock); [ ] no-claim boundary: mechanical close; materiality and treatment judgments stay outside (§0.2).

TESTS: fa-journal kernel tests, fa-reference differential with seeds, CLI binary tests for dry-run/run/status/verify close with robot transcripts.

title: fa-query: the FrankenAccounting GQL profile (FOR PERIOD, AS KNOWN AT, EFFECTIVE AT|BETWEEN, AT BRANCH, AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED, AS CURRENTLY STATED, AS REPORTED IN, CALL fa.*, EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)) rewritten onto substrate GQL, authorization before observation, read procedures bound to the register folds with certificates, the runtime graph (sessions, capabilities, drafts, findings, decision cards, access events) queryable read-only, fa query verb
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): The plan's query language is GQL through the substrate plus the namespaced FrankenAccounting profile (`FOR PERIOD`, `AS KNOWN AT`, `EFFECTIVE AT|BETWEEN`, `AT BRANCH`, `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED`, `AS CURRENTLY STATED`, `AS REPORTED IN <certificate>`, `CALL fa.*`, `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)`), and AGENTS.md requires the system's own runtime (sessions, capabilities, drafts, close runs, findings, decision cards, access events) to be a read-only, access-controlled graph queryable in GQL. At 96d1918 no GQL is executed anywhere (fgdb_gql is used once, for the symbol resolver); `fa query` does not exist. The library's `query` certified read is part of the product shape.

WHAT:
1. `crates/fa-query` (surface layer): the profile parser as a thin front that rewrites the FrankenAccounting clauses into substrate GQL with explicit known-at and effective predicates over the entry/period graph (the clauses are sugar over properties the graph already has: recorded CommitSeq, effective_date, period refs, branch id), refusing anything the profile does not name (exit 3) with the admissible form in the refusal.
2. `CALL fa.*` procedures: `fa.trial_balance`, `fa.balance`, `fa.explain_balance`, `fa.open_items`, `fa.fold` as registered read procedures bound to the same folds fa-registers uses; results carry the coordinate and a certificate when `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)` is requested (the certificate commits to the query text, coordinate and result digest; `fa replay` re-executes).
3. Authorization precedes observation: the capability's caveats (books, accounts subtree, periods, known_at ≤ seq, branch, partial_view) are applied by refusing before query construction in the interim posture (doctrine 8), never as a result filter; whole-entry visibility rules from fa-llx apply.
4. The runtime graph: sessions, capabilities (with revocation), drafts, close runs, findings, decision cards and access events are already or become graph objects; `fa query` can read them under a capability with the `read` op and the matching scope; every read is an access event (journaled, append-only).
5. CLI/library: `Book::query(&cap, text) -> QueryResult`, `fa query "<gql>" --json`, robot events `rows`, `certificate`; byte-deterministic ordering.
6. `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED` / `AS CURRENTLY STATED` and `AS REPORTED IN <certificate>` bind to the palimpsest registers and statement certificates when those land; until then they refuse naming their bead (never a silent fallback).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `fa query "MATCH ... FOR PERIOD 2026-03 AS KNOWN AT 120 CALL fa.trial_balance"` returns rows equal to `fa tb --for 2026-03 --known-at 120` byte-for-byte and `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)` yields a replayable certificate; a query over the runtime graph lists the caller's own session; [ ] planted negatives: a capability scoped to one account subtree refuses a query naming another before any read (no storage observation, proven by a lab VFS read counter); a clause outside the profile is refused with the admissible form; a result-filter implementation (mutation) fails the no-observation test; [ ] proof class: invariant (authorization-before-observation, FA-INV-10) + differential (query vs register folds); [ ] consumers: agents (A6), auditors pinned to a known-at, fa-mcp resources, the dogfooded runtime graph; [ ] no-claim boundary: the profile proves parity with the folds for the covered procedures, not general GQL completeness.

TESTS: parser goldens, kernel-level authorization tests with the read counter, differential vs fa-registers and fa-reference, CLI binary tests with query text and coordinate logged.

title: fa-notary/fa-verify boundary: producer inlines documents the standalone verifier refuses (16 MiB stub limit vs 64 MiB external storage); add producer admission limits FA-REF-129 BUNDLE_LIMIT (inline > 16 MiB, balance count > 4096) with early validation before cited-document reads

title: Reference-oracle coverage for the owner's new report families and allocations: independent limb mul/div in fa-reference, brute-force cash flow / aging / roll-forward / GL detail / allocation laws, and a multi-seed, multi-unit, multi-entity differential campaign
description:
## Why
The new families (allocations, cash flow ×4, aging + reconciliation + portfolio, roll-forward, GL detail)
have no oracle at all; fa-reference's limb `Int` has add/sub only (no mul/div), so allocation, FX and
valuation have no independent check (FA-INV-06); the core differential uses ONE fixed seed, one unit
(USD), 3 accounts, 4 dates. The reporting audit found two real semantic defects (cash-flow gross, aging
allocation) that an oracle would have caught.

## What to build
1. fa-reference: independent schoolbook limb multiplication and long division (std only), checked by
   property tests against fa-money AND fgdb-bigint in tests (the oracle never imports them at runtime).
2. Naïve allocation laws (LargestRemainder, ProRataResidualToNamed, EqualSplit, Waterfall) from the
   registry rows; naïve cash flow (direct by literal classification, indirect by literal bridge), aging by
   literal date buckets, roll-forward and GL detail as literal per-account sorted folds.
3. Differential campaign: ≥ 32 seeds × {1, 3 units} × {1, 2 entities} × {3, 12 accounts} × 3 calendar kinds,
   generated intent histories (posts, holds, voids, reversals, settlements, allocations, migrations), every
   report family compared at several (known_at, effective) coordinates; failures print the seed and a
   minimized history.

## Acceptance
All families agree on all seeds; a planted kernel mutation in each family is killed by at least one seed
(record in the mutant ledger fa-9km9).

## Tests & logging
Campaign test with `FA_SEEDS` env override; per-seed log line (seed, steps, families, mismatches=0).
close_reason: Implemented naive Int mul/div_rem and std+fa-time+Int reference-oracle implementations for allocation laws (largest_remainder, pro_rata_residual_to_named across all 9 rounding modes, equal_split_residual_first, waterfall) and report families (roll_forward, gl_detail, effective-date aging + control TB reconciliation, direct_cash_flow, indirect_cash_flow) in crates/fa-reference/src/reports.rs, with multi-seed differential campaign and planted-mutation kill checks in crates/fa/tests/report_oracle.rs.

title: Evidence intake pipeline: derived text Documents from owner tools run as subprocess graders (franken_ocr focr, franken_whisper fw robot), deterministic PDF text-layer extraction, DERIVED_FROM lineage, honest grading
description:
WHY: Bet A3 is only as strong as what can become a Document. title: TLA+ model of the merge train: trunk only advances to a tree with a green verdict; every queued candidate eventually lands or is ejected naming its failing step
description:

title: Outsider-verifiable certified reports: `fa bundle produce --certificate <oid>` packages a TB/statement certificate with scope-complete proofs of its closure; `fa-verify report` recomputes every line offline
description:
## Why (the A3+A5 join — the regulator/court feature)
Certificates replay only inside the book (native certified reads + the book's registries). An outsider
can verify inclusion, prefix and one account/unit balance, but not a whole trial balance or statement.
The plan's promise: "Any balance is verifiable offline"; "every report replays byte-for-byte from its
certificate"; examiners and courts receive certificates.

## What to build
- Bundle profile `report`: the certificate, its RegistryEpoch texts (see the certificate-portability
  bead), the complete record set for its closure with scope-completeness proofs (scope index) or the
  complete-prefix fallback, and the canonical report bytes.
- fa-verify `report <bundle> --checkpoint <signed> --key <pk>`: recompute TB (stock/activity/as-of) and
  the two statement kinds with its own std-only fold, compare to the certified bytes, report per-line
  predicates. Shares the migration-visibility law with fa-e00's fix.
- Equivalence campaign: in-book replay == fa-verify report over generated histories.

## Tests
Golden bundle; tampered line detected; omitted record detected by scope proof; campaign green.
acceptance_criteria: A certified TB and a statement verify offline with fa-verify; campaign green.

description:
WHY: plan §5.3 "A balance read at the head is register(cell) ⊕ fold(legs of cell in (watermark, head]) … reads are O(1) at the watermark plus a bounded tail scan"; the maintainer "run[s] as a supervised region woken by fad after each commit"; §17 gates (balance read p99 < 50 µs; TB of 100k accounts < 200 ms). **What landed:**

It point-reads the registers of the chart's accounts in every unit their policies admit, and requires the assembled cells to reproduce the state's fold digest. It then folds only the entries committed after the cursor, through `apply_tail`, which is now shared with `prepare_advance` so both apply one law.
- It writes nothing and repairs nothing. In any doubtful case it returns None: no or damaged state, a drifted cell, a retired delta window, or a tail that needs a rebuild. Retired cells (label removed by `materialize_batch`) are skipped.
- `trial_balance_served` sums the head folds of every period that ends on or before the selection's last day. A straddling period, or a period with postings but no servable cells, falls back to the literal fold.
- `period_activity_served` does the same for the selected periods.
- `trial_balance_from_sums` is the row builder both paths share.
- `Served::{Maintained(period, served_at, tail_entries), Literal(reason)}` with `tail_length()` is the plan §17 disclosure.

- [x] Planted negative, cache drift: `a_drifted_register_cell_is_never_served`. One forged register amount makes the read fall back to the literal fold, which still returns the right rows, and `verify registers` reports it.
- [~] Complexity witness: `a_maintained_head_read_decodes_only_its_tail_regardless_of_unrelated_history`. After maintenance catches up, a March read decodes 0 entries despite 300 April postings; one new March posting decodes once per maintained contributing period (2). This counts decoded entries, not substrate reads, because the pinned substrate has no read counter.
- [ ] Not claimed: a self-consistent but wrong cache (a maintainer bug that skipped a delta yet wrote matching digests) is detected by `verify registers`, not by the read.

comments.text:
## 2026-10-19 (claude-opus-5-5): scoping notes; not started, still OPEN

Read before any code. The design points below need a decision first.

1. **Two lifecycles disagree.** Plan §8.3 and Appendix B (`OpenRestatementCase` … `DiscloseCase`) define Proposed → Determined → Rehearsed → Approved → Posted → Disclosed → Closed. The pure model in `crates/fa-palimpsest/src/lib.rs` (`RestatementCaseState`) is Open → Approved → Applied → Closed: it has no determination, rehearsal or disclosure, and records approvals inside the case (`approvers: Vec<Id128>`). Plan §4.6 / Appendix A say approvals are `Approval` payload objects that bind the body's `proposal_digest`, never case fields. A journaled slice should follow the plan; the palimpsest type is then either reworked or retired (it has no journal caller today).
2. **Appendix A's body timing is ambiguous.** The immutable `RestatementCase` body carries `determination: Option<{day, authority_oid}>` and `proposal_digest`, but both become known only after later transitions (Determined; the approved effect manifest of §8.3). One consistent reading:
   - The body is fixed at open: kind, periods_affected, narrative_oid, and the determination if it was already made.
   - The Determine transition carries `{day, authority document}` in its proof_refs.
   - The Approved transition names the ordered effect manifest, and the approvals bind its digest.
   Needs an owner ruling before any durable tag is minted.
3. **Rehearsal can reuse what exists.** The scenario machinery (`fa scenario fork|run|diff --certify`, the `fa:scenario-diff-certificate:v1` replay, fa-k07b) already produces an as-reported-vs-counterfactual diff certificate over a scratch replay. A case rehearsal could be a scenario forked at the case's as-reported sequence with its diff certificate attached to Rehearsed. The IAS 1.40A third balance sheet and the ASC 250-10-50-7 table would then be statement-level views over that diff.
4. **Today's kernel.** Revision, Restatement and PriorPeriodAdjustment are refused CLASS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED (fa-journal post.rs `not_implemented`). The admissibility rows with `note = "case"` (`with:restate,1|2`) are declared but unreachable, and denial.rs names the missing case for Locked reopen. Slice 2 must add the case qualifier to the reference oracle as well (G0-03 four-way equality).
5. **Scoreboard.** WF-RQ-09 runs `fa case open --kind Restatement --periods FY2025-P12`, with no narrative and no reason. The README example adds `--narrative restatement-memo.pdf`.

Suggested slice order:
1. A journaled case body plus open, determine, show and list. That flips WF-RQ-09, and the step description must say that posting is not yet available.
2. Rehearse via a scenario plus the diff certificate.
3. Approval objects plus dual control (`restate`).
4. Posted as one write_ordered batch with case-gated admission in kernel and oracle.
5. Disclose and Close.

title: One-writer discipline mechanized: pre-push guard (main/staging need a verdict note for the exact tree), trunk_audit step, claim-before-code check in the train, WIP limit and stale-claim report
description:
## Why
33 owner commits reached main without compiling; 7.3K swarm lines were withdrawn because the owner
implemented beads the swarm held in_progress (fa-cqk, fa-avx, fa-nnm, fa-23r, fa-d08, fa-zxm); one
agent held 16 in_progress claims; a 6.2K-line WIP was re-squashed six times chasing moving tips.

## What to build
1. scripts/hooks/pre-push (installed by scripts/install-hooks.sh; documented in AGENTS.md): refuses a
   push to refs/heads/main or refs/heads/staging unless the pushed tip has a green verdict note
   (refs/notes/verdicts) for its exact tree; pushes to refs/heads/train/* are always allowed
   (toolchain-less sessions push there).
2. scripts/trunk_audit.sh, a check.sh step: lists trunk commits since the RECON-2 merge without a green
   verdict note; must be empty.
3. Claim-before-code: merge_train.sh refuses a candidate whose commit messages name a bead whose
   assignee is someone other than the candidate's author (reads the beads DB/JSONL).
4. scripts/stale_claims.sh: in_progress beads with no commit mentioning them in 24h and agents holding
   more than 2 in_progress beads; printed by `fa-triage`-style tooling for the orchestrator.

## Tests & logging
Hook test with a temp repo: push without note refused with an actionable message; with note allowed;
train refuses a candidate for a bead assigned elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Hook installed and tested; trunk_audit green after RECON-2; claim check refuses the planted case.
close_reason: Implemented scripts/hooks/pre-push, scripts/install-hooks.sh, scripts/trunk_audit.sh, scripts/stale_claims.sh, and --check-claims in scripts/merge_train.sh; verified with scripts/tests/batch_and_discipline_selftest.sh.

title: Capacity envelope: every hard limit in the code is a registered, derived row in limits.toml with a boundary test at cap−1/cap/cap+1 that ends in a catalog refusal naming the limit and the fix — never a raw kernel/storage error, never a cap counted before filtering
description:
## Why (found 2026-10-14)
Limits surface one at a time, at scale, as raw errors:
- substrate row 16,384 B (Entries fa-fdt, Certificates, Documents, allocation bases → BLOB);
- certification native-read budget 10M records / 1M rows (crates/fa/src/certificate.rs:449-453) ⇒ books
  above ~1M entries cannot certify;
- aging portfolio cap 100k rows counted BEFORE filtering (portfolio.rs:219-224, 302) ⇒ ~50k-entry books
  refused even for one account;
- indirect cash bridge refuses > 4,096 non-cash leaves;
- MAX_POSTING_TARGETS = 1,024 is unreachable (row cap ≈ 200 targets);
- proof files capped at 64 MiB ≈ 450k journal entries (envelope-per-leaf);
- daemon frame bound for inline proofs; Lantern duplicate groups capped at 4,096 (untested).
None of these is in limits.toml with a derivation; most have no boundary test; several report exit 5
(foundation failure) for what is a capacity refusal.

## What to build
1. Inventory (std-only tripwire): every `const MAX_*`, budget constant and `RowExceedsStorageLimit` path in
   crates/ maps to a limits.toml row {name, value, unit, derivation (formula from substrate/registry
   constants), refusal code, owner bead}; the tripwire fails on an unregistered constant.
2. Each row gets a boundary test (cap−1 admitted, cap admitted or refused per the row, cap+1 refused with the
   catalog code, exit 3 or 7 as registered, never 5) and a fix text naming the alternative (paging, batch,
   scope narrowing, blob route).
3. Caps count after filtering (the portfolio cap applies to the selected accounts).
4. Raise or remove caps whose only reason was the row size once BLOB lands; record each change.

## Acceptance
Tripwire green; every row has its three boundary tests; no capacity condition exits 5.

## Tests & logging
A generated boundary-test table; each case logs (limit, size, expected, actual, refusal id).

title: Gate scoreboard: G0, Genesis, G1–G4 exit criteria as executable checks run against the real binaries in check.sh, reporting works / refused-with-bead / absent-with-bead per criterion
description:
## Why
Gates are declared by hand today ("Gate G0 and the full Genesis acceptance criteria remain open").
The plan's §19 criteria are concrete and mostly mechanical. A scoreboard computed from the binary on
every gate makes progress measurable (anti-ceremony: scoreboard deltas, not bead counts) and makes the
next reality check a diff. Companion to fa-e9z (README quick example + §15.6 workflows).

## Criteria to encode (from the plan, §19)
G0: every §18.2 registry present (37; 16 present at the check); FA-INV spine with checkers; threat
model; admissibility exhaustive test; catalogs frozen at major 1; object_schemas with golden vectors;
bundle/certificate schemas externally_verifiable; robot schema pin; operation_costs.toml with the
derivability law; foundation rows checked; tools/registry-check green; check.sh verdict contract;
README/AGENTS sync.
Genesis: create book under lab; chart+calendar as journaled schema effects; PostEntry through
admit→resolve→laws→plan→commit; legs equal payload (real checker); maintainer advances and
balance = fold; crash at plan↔commit, commit↔ack, delta↔watermark and recover; `fa tb --json`
certified; `fa verify registers` green; unbalanced → exit 3 with per-unit imbalance; Closed → exit 7
with the matrix cell; `fa replay` reproduces TB bytes; no stub register/post-filter capability/float/
wall clock.
G1: Genesis green under lab (1,000 seeds) and live; Genesis clause set live; registers verified by fold
on every fixture; idempotency and batches under crash; reference differential over generated
histories; triage/post/tb/explain balance/doctor at the Polish Bar; fa-verify verifies a produced
bundle of the Genesis book. G2–G4 per §19 (period law in both race orders, AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED / AS
REPORTED IN, netting and restatement cases, witnessed checkpoints, Beancount/hledger differential,
Canon corpora, confirm_plan; G3 verb parity, fresh-context agents, FA-INV-10 full, statements +
consolidation certified, Lantern precision/recall, ADS/SAF-T, demo, gauntlet scorecards; G4 manifests,
conformance matrices, all clauses live or absent, static fa-verify release).

## What to build
scripts/gate_scoreboard (Rust test binary or std-only tool) with one check per criterion, each mapped
to its bead id; output a table + JSON; check.sh step reports the counts (never fails the gate on
"absent-with-bead", fails on "regressed"). README status section generated from it.

## Tests & logging
Each check logs the command it ran, exit code, and the event it expected; regressions (works → not)
fail the step.
acceptance_criteria: Scoreboard runs in check.sh; README status is generated from it; at least the Genesis and G1 criteria are executable checks.
close_reason: Implemented Convergence Gate Scoreboard in registries/scoreboard.toml (18 gate criteria across G0, Genesis, G1-G4), fixed period_transitions IN_PERIOD vertex label filtering bug in fa-journal uncovered by G2-01 after registers advance, and verified all scoreboard, fa-registry, and registry-check tests pass

title: Decision-card framework: a journaled, replayable DecisionCard (state space, candidates, features, expected-benefit interval, pinned deterministic fallback, policy epoch) used by every adaptive decision
description:
## Why (AGENTS.md "Adaptive-Decision Contract"; Core)
Every adaptive decision — bank-match heuristics, forensic thresholds, sampling stratification, register
checkpoint cadence, bundle evidence inlining, and (Track 0) the merge train's batch size — must emit a
replayable decision card under a versioned policy epoch with a deterministic pinned fallback, and no card
may change a committed amount. Nothing implements this today; parameters are hard-coded defaults.

## What to build
- A small crate or module (laws layer, pure, stripped Cx): DecisionCard { policy_epoch, decision_kind,
  state (canonical bytes), candidates, features, chosen, expected_benefit_interval, fallback, reason }.
- Recording: journaled when the decision affects book state (as a control/metadata object) or logged
  with its digest when it affects only a process (the train); replay recomputes the decision bit-for-bit
  in the lab runtime.
- Policy registry rows per decision kind; learned scores allowed only as advisory features.
- First consumers: register checkpoint cadence (fa-vn4), Lantern thresholds (calibration bead),
  dry-run warning thresholds, train batch size.

## Tests
Replay determinism; fallback chosen when the policy is absent or the interval is wide; a card can never
alter a committed amount (property over generated decisions).
acceptance_criteria: Framework landed with two consumers; replay test green.
close_reason: Implemented replayable DecisionCard framework in fa-policy::decision (re-exported in fa-steward and fa) with two live consumers (register checkpoint cadence in fa-registers and procedure threshold calibration in fa-lantern) plus CLI E2E replay test.

title: Period-transition control date law: derive the control's effective date from the period (close = last_day, reopen/restate = the registered boundary) instead of accepting a caller date — oracle rule, differential transition_day update, transition_proposal digest/approval/facade/CLI signature change
description: WHY (WhiteCreek 3568 (C) / RubyMoose, MistyPlateau 3574, 2026-10-11): today transition_period takes a caller-supplied effective date and copies it into the period control record; fa-registers/tests/differential.rs dates every transition 2026-01-01 (transition_day(), ~line 959; Feb/Mar/Apr transitions at ~1268) and the reference oracle admits them, so a control for March can carry Apr 15. Slice 1 of fa-llx closes the authorization hole only (the caller date joins the scoped token's footprint: its period is added to reach and through = max(period.last_day, caller date), refused in admit_within before any read). The period-law question — what date a period control legitimately carries — is a separate rule with its own oracle and differential update, and it changes transition_proposal digests, approvals and the facade/CLI signatures, so it is not a scope-slice change. WHAT: (1) decide and register the law in the plan's period section (A2) and registries/entry_classes.toml control rows: a period transition control is dated by the period it transitions (close → last_day; reopen/restate → the registered boundary), never by the caller; book-scoped controls stay undated (plan §7.1); (2) fa-reference oracle rule + fa-registers differential: drop transition_day(), derive from the period, and add a planted negative (a caller-dated transition is a usage refusal, exit 2, before any read); (3) transition_proposal: remove the date input, re-derive the digest, update approvals that bind it, the facade signature and the fa-cli verb (verbs.toml row + robot-schema fixture re-pin); (4) migration note: no users, no shim; the durable control encoding changes in place (fa-bvx owns the encoding). ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: every period control on a fresh book is dated inside its own period and the differential is green with no transition_day(); [ ] planted negative: a caller-dated transition is refused with exit 2 and an unchanged frontier; a control dated outside its period cannot be constructed (type-level) ; [ ] proof class: invariant (period law at commit) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-llx footprint (its max(last_day, caller) term becomes last_day), fa-bvx lifecycle projections, Almanac period state machine, CLI/MCP transition verbs; [ ] no-claim boundary: this bead fixes the date law of period controls, not the admissibility matrix rows (Appendix C) themselves.
close_reason: Landed 4eb850a7 on main 491003a2: the period dates its own PeriodControl entries (Open on its first day, later transitions on its last), no caller supplies a date, verify_periods detects a misdated control. Gate sl9 on the tip: clippy green; tests 2434 passed, 4 failed, all inherited from main (see the comment).

comments.author: StormyLion
comments.text:
## 2026-10-20 (StormyLion, claude-opus-5-5): implemented in 4eb850a7; landed on main at main/master 491003a2. Gates below.

**The law (plan §7.3, now registered in the plan):** the period it transitions dates every PeriodControl entry. An Open is dated on the period's first day; every later transition (soft close, close, lock, reopen) is dated on its last day. No caller supplies a date.

**Acceptance, item by item:**
- Positive: every period control is dated inside its own period. The fa-registers differential asserts the kernel's journaled date equals the oracle's independently computed `transition_date` for every committed transition in the generated walk and in `close_and_maybe_lock`. `transition_day()` is gone; book-scoped controls keep `control_day()`.
- Planted negative, CLI: `fa period soft-close|close FY2026-P03 --date 2026-04-15` exits 2 with the head unchanged (`period_controls_are_dated_by_their_period_never_by_the_caller`, fa-cli plans.rs). The journaled controls are dated 03-01, 03-31 and 03-31.
- Type-level: `transition_proposal(book, &PeriodDef, from, to, ...)` takes no date, so a misdated control cannot be built through the API.
- Detection: `verify_periods` reports an off-law date as drift. Planted negative `misdated-control` in fa-journal genesis.rs: March's Open is re-sealed one day later, still inside March, with consistent mirrors, and it is the only drift reported.
- fa-llx footprint: a transition's reach is exactly its period, through the period's last day. The `max(last_day, caller date)` term and the second period it could add are gone.
- Plan file format `fa:period-plan` v2: the date field is removed and v1 is refused. `TransitionPlan::proposal`/`proposal_digest` and `Book::plan_digest` refuse a plan naming a period the calendar lacks, returning an Outcome.
- fa-gen: `GenTransition.effective_date` is removed. It dated P01 soft closes on 02-01, outside P01.

**Tests changed (disclosed in the commit trailer):** the policy.rs footprint test now probes the law's date. The idempotency test's "different date conflicts" probe became "different reason conflicts".

- Workspace `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: rc=0, with the `Finished` and `exit=0` markers.

Both are hard-coded counts that d861490d (fa-y4v) grew by its 8 new procedures. Reported to the fa-y4v owner in mail.
  - fa-cli `retained_trial_balances_replay_exactly_and_report_later_relevant_entries` (exit 2 vs 8) and fa-mcp `bank_history_over_stdio_preserves_releases_and_source_authority` (3 vs 7). Both are red with the same assertions on MaroonCat's de229bf3 baseline.

title: Formal anchors: Lean lanes (Amount group laws, rounding bounds generated from rounding_laws.toml, allocation conservation, reversal balance preservation, netting, period state machine, bitemporal visibility) and TLA+ models (close DAG under crashes, two-phase with expiry, draft promotion vs moving trunk, restatement lifecycle) with stated bounds, mapped to invariants.toml clauses
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): The verification ladder names scoped formal anchors: Lean for `Amount` group laws, rounding bounds, allocation conservation, balance-law preservation under supersession, netting, bitemporal visibility, the period state machine and escrow bounds; TLA+ for the close DAG under crashes, the restatement case life cycle, two-phase with expiry, and draft promotion against a moving trunk. W1 lists "Lean lanes" for fa-money. At 96d1918 there are no Lean or TLA+ artifacts (no directories, 0 hits). fa-uqq (independent `fln check-olean` re-check) presumes anchors that do not exist, so it is blocked on this bead.

WHAT:
1. `formal/lean/` (not a Cargo member): a Lean 4 project with one module per anchor: `Amount` as an additive group at a fixed scale with checked overflow modeled as `Option`; the nine rounding laws of `registries/rounding_laws.toml` with the half-ulp error bound (the registry is the single source: a generator emits the Lean definitions from the TOML and a test diffs them); largest-remainder allocation conserves the total and bounds each residual; a `Reverses` side-swap preserves the per-unit balance law; netting laws (when fa-palimpsest slice 2 lands) net to the stated result; the period state machine of fa-time/src/period.rs as a transition relation with the plan's reachability facts; bitemporal visibility (known-at monotonicity); escrow bounds (dormant until escrow exists).
2. `formal/tla/`: TLA+ specs with TLC configs and stated bounds: close DAG under crashes (W3), two-phase holds with the expiry sweep and the identity race (fa-ctf), draft promotion against a moving trunk (fa-s7x), restatement case life cycle (fa-palimpsest slice 2); each spec's invariants map to FA-INV clause ids in `registries/invariants.toml` with evidence class `proof` (Lean) or `bounded_model` (TLA+, with the bound).
3. Cross-check with code: for every Lean theorem about a registry row, a Rust test exercises the same concrete vectors; the TLA+ models' action names mirror the kernel's pipeline barrier names used by fa-sim-harness crash points.
4. A `scripts/check.sh` step `formal` that builds the Lean project and runs the bounded TLC configs when the toolchains are present, and emits UNRUN (never PASS) when they are absent.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `lake build` succeeds with every theorem closed (no `sorry`), the TLC runs finish within their stated bounds with no invariant violation, and each anchor is listed in invariants.toml with its clause; [ ] planted negatives: weakening the Lean rounding bound to one ulp fails the generated-definition diff; a TLA+ model with the identity-uniqueness guard removed reports the double-release counterexample; [ ] proof class: proof (Lean) and bounded_model (TLA+), both stated per anchor; [ ] consumers: fa-uqq, the G1/G2 invariant reviews, the papers; [ ] no-claim boundary: every model states its bounds; nothing here claims the Rust code is verified, only that the stated laws are consistent and the code's vectors agree.

TESTS: the generated-definition diff test and the vector cross-checks in Rust; TLC logs archived per run with the bound and the state count.
close_reason: Implemented Lean 4 formal anchor modules (Amount group laws, RoundingLaws generated from registries/rounding_laws.toml, Allocation conservation, Supersession reversal/netting laws, Period state machine, Bitemporal visibility, Escrow bounds) in formal/lean/, TLA+ bounded models with TLC configs in formal/tla/, and Rust generator diff + concrete vector cross-checks + exhaustive state-space exploration in crates/fa-money/tests/formal_anchors.rs.
