title: Report certificates bind raw registry text: a comment-only registry edit changes every certificate digest and makes every retained certificate refuse replay (FA-INV-11)
description:
## Why
Report certificates commit to the registries they were computed under (`registry_digest`, crates/fa/src/certificate.rs ~391-431), but they hash each registry's RAW TEXT, comments included.

Observed on 2026-10-16:
- Two edits moved the cross-target trial-balance certificate pin:
  - a comment-only rewrite of registries/account_types.toml (6893ac3d, fa-a57x);
  - an additive symbols.toml row (1ecc2507, fa-yyl3).
- b1a4f34d's account_types/units changes moved it again.

The same mechanism has two consequences:
1. **Every retained certificate refuses replay** after any registry edit, comment typos included. certificate.rs ~987 compares the registry digest. That breaks FA-INV-11 ("`fa replay <certificate>` ⇒ byte-identical re-execution") for every book whose binary is upgraded, even when no accounting rule changed.
2. **Pins churn on cosmetic edits.** Every cross-target and golden pin over certificates moves on cosmetic edits, which trains everyone to regenerate goldens reflexively (a named reward-hacking pattern).

## What to build
1. Commit to the **parsed, canonical registry content** each report depends on, not file bytes. Use a versioned canonical encoding per registry, with comments and whitespace excluded. Tag it with the registry `schema_version` so a semantic change still changes the digest.
2. A certificate binds only the registries its computation reads, by name plus canonical digest. Today all hashed registries are bound.
3. Replay of a certificate produced under an older registry digest:
   - If the binary still carries a registry whose canonical digest equals the recorded one, replay proceeds.
   - Otherwise it is a typed refusal naming the registry and both digests, never an opaque mismatch.
4. Migration note for already-retained certificates: they bind raw-text digests. Keep a v-tagged verifier for them, or document the one-time break. Do not silently reinterpret.

## Acceptance
- Planted: a comment-only edit to account_types.toml leaves the TB/BS/IS certificate digests and replay unchanged.
- Planted: changing an account type's normal side changes the digest, and replay is refused with the typed refusal.
- Cross-target pins re-measured once under the new encoding, with the commit naming why.
- FA-INV-11 clause updated with these negatives.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Landed on main at 923e929d (2026-10-18, claude-opus-5-5) in commit f704b85e (fix(certificates)). Gates: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` exit 0 at 923e929d (2157 passed, 0 failed, 168 test binaries; vmi1149989, 2026-10-18T16:37Z); `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0 at fda5f40f (vmi1153651, 0 warnings), and on the crates changed since (fa, fa-cli, fa-registry) exit 0 (hz2, 0 warnings) at 923e929d.

**What works:**
- **Canonical encoding:** fa-registry Document::canonical_bytes (fa:registry-document:v1) is an injective encoding of the parsed content. Comments, blank lines, spacing, key order and integer separators do not reach it; every key, value, table name and array row (in order) does, schema_version included.
- **v2 closures:** report and procedure certificates bind a v2 closure over each bound registry's canonical digest.
- **Comment edits:** a comment-only or layout-only edit to account_types.toml leaves the closure unchanged, as do the TB/BS/IS certificates and their replay (planted test). A flipped normal side moves the closure.
- **Retained certificates:** a certificate retained before this change carries the v1 raw-text closure, and replay still accepts it (tested for the trial balance and open items), so nothing retained breaks. New certificates never carry v1.
- **Typed refusal:** a closure this executable does not carry is FA-REF-159 CERTIFICATE_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE (exit environment). It names the recorded closure, this executable's closure and the registries it covers, instead of the old opaque FA-REF-150 text.
- **Pins:** the cross-target pins were re-measured once (tb/bs/is certificates only; the fold, statement bytes and bundle are unchanged). They no longer move on cosmetic edits.

**Not done (the bead stays open):**
- Naming the one registry that differs: the certificate holds a single closure digest, so this needs per-registry digests in the format. That belongs with fa-oimc's unified certificate contract.
- Narrowing each report's bound set to the registries its computation reads. The set is unchanged and conservative; replay still compares the output bytes.
- FA-INV-11.report-replay is dormant (activated by fa-9ae), so the new negatives are not registered in invariants.toml yet.

title: Unit evolution: journaled unit table as the runtime source, unit versions (USD@2 → USD@4) with exact ScaleConversion laws and Redenomination control records; historical mantissas never reinterpreted (FA-INV-02.unit-version)
description:
WHY: plan §4.4: "A UnitId is immutable, scale included. A precision change creates a new unit version with a registered exact ScaleConversion law (× 10^k) and a Redenomination control record; … folds across versions apply the law at read time, recording it in the certificate. An economic redenomination is a different unit with a conversion rate document". At e606b46 any rate converts between unit versions (crates/fa-money/src/amount.rs:686-694), the unit table is not journaled as the runtime source (fa-nnm), and FA-INV-02.unit-version is dormant; README says "Journaled unit evolution … remain[s] unfinished (fa-p7r)" — fa-p7r is the spec bead; this is the implementation.

WHAT: SchemaChange{kind=unit_version} control adding a unit version with its ScaleConversion law (exact power of ten, lossless); registry of conversion laws between versions; folds that span versions convert at read time under the law and list it in the certificate (fa-cqk); posting into a superseded version after its successor's effective date refused with the successor named; `fa unit list|add|version --json`.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: USD@2 → USD@4 at a date; a tb spanning the change folds exactly and names the law; [ ] planted negatives: non-power-of-ten scale conversion refused; posting USD@2 after cutover refused; reinterpreting a historical mantissa impossible (property test: every historical cell identical before/after the version change); [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-02.unit-version live) ; [ ] consumers: crypto/commodity books, fa-s3c; [ ] no-claim boundary: precision changes only; redenomination is a rate-document conversion.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 2026-10-20 (StormyLion, claude-opus-5-5): design findings, read-only at origin/main de229bf3. Not started; still open

These are the five decisions that make this bead multi-day:

1. **A book's unit table is sealed at genesis.**
   - genesis journals the binary registry's units as Unit vertices.
   - It pins `Book.unit_table_digest` on the root.
   - `fa_journal::genesis::read_units` refuses any journaled unit that the binary registry (units.toml) lacks.
   - A version added later therefore needs a second source, verified by its own control rather than by the root digest. That control is `SchemaChange` kind 14 (kinds 1-13 are taken: chart 1-4, REA 5-11, closing routes 12, period births 13).
   - `fa/src/certificate.rs` compares the root digest with `unit_table_digest(&book.units)`, so certificates must bind the genesis table plus the version controls, not a recomputed whole table.

2. **The successor must not enter units.toml.**
   - Adding `USD@v1` there would put it in every new book's genesis table.
   - Unversioned parsing ("1.23 USD") resolves to the highest registered version (fa-money `rendering_preserves_historical_unit_versions`), so every fixture would silently switch scale.
   - The version is therefore book-local: the next dense UnitId after the book's table.

3. **Parsing becomes date-dependent.**
   - "USD" must mean the version in force at the entry's effective date.
   - Every intent and typed-document parser needs the date: fa-cli intents, typed verbs, allocation, bank and migration imports, and MCP.
   - Otherwise backdated entries must spell `USD@v0`.

4. **Account unit policy.**
   - `UnitPolicy::Single(UnitId)` pins one version.
   - Either the redenomination control re-points accounts, or policies match by code.
   - Pick one before the kernel check "posting into a superseded version after the successor's date is refused, naming the successor".

5. **Cross-version folds.**
   - TB, statements and certificates must convert old-version cells by the ×10^k law at read time and name the law.
   - Report rows are keyed by `unit_id` today.

Suggested first slice: items 1 and 4, plus `fa unit list`, plus the posting refusal. Leave parsing (item 3) and folds (item 5) to later slices.

title: Docket slice 2: custody chains, ImportRun control records with receipt hashes, external document storage behind public commitments with verified reads, redaction contracts as derived objects, retention holds blocking erasure and expiry
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Docket's first slice (fa-lp6) delivers content-addressed documents, chunk-Merkle commitments, evidence minimums and `EVIDENCED_BY`; fa-journal/src/evidence.rs lists custody, import receipts, bank lines, external storage and redaction as "later slices". Plan §9 and W4 require them before Gate G2 ("documents, custody, attestations, balance assertions"). fa-v74 (subject keys) and fa-646 (intake pipeline) touch adjacent ground; fa-j9t is the spec-side contract bead. This bead is the code.

WHAT:
1. Custody chain: every document carries an immutable `Custody` lineage (received-from principal/system, received-at CommitSeq, transfer events as journaled objects), queryable as `fa document custody <oid>`; a document cannot be cited by an entry unless its custody chain is complete to a registered intake source.
2. Import receipts: `ImportRun` as a control record (legs = []) with the source descriptor, byte count, document count, the Merkle root over the imported documents' oids, and a receipt hash the external party can keep; `fa import receipt <run>`; receipts are what fa-ff6 and fa-646 must produce.
3. External document storage: documents above the inline threshold store bytes outside the journal under a registered store descriptor with the public commitment (chunk-tree root) inline; reads verify the commitment on every access; a missing external blob is a typed refusal (exit 5, foundation/I-O) and never a silent null; the plan's "public commitments" let a bundle prove a document without shipping it.
4. Redaction contracts: `redaction = <contract>` capability caveat; a redacted view of a document is a derived object with its own commitment and lineage to the original; redaction never changes an amount or an entry (erasure-leaves-amounts-intact oracle); subject-key erasure (fa-v74) composes with this.
5. Retention holds: `RetentionHold` control records that block erasure cuts and expiry sweeps for the held subjects; releases are journaled.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an import run of N documents produces a receipt whose root recomputes from the oids; an external document reads back byte-identically with the commitment verified; a redacted view omits the field and keeps the entry's amounts; a hold blocks an erasure cut with a refusal naming the hold; [ ] planted negatives: a tampered external blob is refused on read (exit 8); a document without custody cannot be cited (refusal names the missing link); an erasure cut under a hold is refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (commitments, lineage) + differential (fa-reference naive custody/receipt model); [ ] consumers: fa-ff6, fa-646, fa-v74, bundles (A3), G2; [ ] no-claim boundary: receipts prove what was imported, not that the source was truthful.

title: Accumulator maintained in commit order off the write path: an MMR advanced by fad from delta_since (O(log n) append, RFC 9162-style O(log n) inclusion/consistency proofs) replacing whole-prefix rescans
description:
## Why (plan §13.2)
Today `checkpoint` (fa-notary state.rs ~308) and every proof re-read the whole prefix with
`db.vertices_at(seq)` and rebuild the tree; `verify_accumulator` rebuilds every state on the chain
(O(states x vertices)). Plan: a journal-level accumulator maintained in commit order, off the write path.

## What to build
- Merkle Mountain Range over entry leaves in commit order: peaks persisted as AccumulatorState control
  records at each checkpoint; fad advances it from delta_since after commits (supervised, cancellable);
  append O(log n).
- Inclusion proofs (leaf → peak → bagged root) and consistency proofs between checkpoints of O(log n)
  size; fa-verify verifies them with its own BLAKE3; golden vectors.
- Equivalence campaign: MMR roots/proofs vs the current rebuild implementation over generated histories
  (existing proofs must remain verifiable or carry a format version bump with both verifiers).

## Tests
Golden vectors; equivalence campaign >= 8 seeds; checkpoint cost scaling test (log-shaped).
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint and proof generation no longer rescan the prefix; formats pinned; campaign green.

title: Bind every verdict to an exact tree: per-step verdict manifests keyed by tree hash (a split run is one verdict iff every step PASSed on that tree), scripts/local_proof.sh + merge_train.sh + br_sync.sh adopted from the substrate, verdicts as git notes; bead closes cite a manifest id
description:
WHY: AGENTS.md "A green scripts/check.sh in a dirty tree is not a verdict"; local_proof.sh "runs scripts/check.sh against the exact committed tree, refuses a dirty worktree, and writes a manifest binding the verdict to that commit and tree hash"; merge_train.sh is "the only path from staging to main". At e606b46 none of local_proof.sh, merge_train.sh, br_sync.sh, check-forbidden-deps.sh exist, there are no git notes refs, and the last literal single check.sh exit 0 is a7203b82 (2026-10-10 22:24), 45 commits before the tip; the tip has clippy + tests on an equivalent tree but no check.sh run. Because rch's daemon queue cap (300 s) and 1800/3600/7200 s kill limits routinely leave steps UNRUN, the swarm has closed beads on stitched runs (a full run with 13 PASS / 2 UNRUN plus a separate `--quick` run at the same tree, e.g. 3a4349f; commit 5de0c4b itself notes "their concatenation is not a new all-fifteen-step verdict"). The doctrine is right; the tooling to satisfy it honestly under a saturated fleet is missing, which is what pushes people into stitching.

WHAT (the ambitious, honest fix): (1) check.sh writes a per-step verdict record `{step, status PASS|FAIL|UNRUN, tree_hash, toolchain, worker, started, finished, log_digest}` to a manifest; (2) `scripts/local_proof.sh <commit>` refuses a dirty tree, runs only the steps not already PASSed for that exact tree hash and toolchain, and emits a final verdict manifest iff every registered step has a PASS record for that tree — so a split run IS one verdict by construction, with no human stitching; any FAIL for that tree invalidates the manifest; (3) manifests stored as git notes under refs/notes/fa-verdict keyed by commit, and mirrored to origin; (4) `scripts/merge_train.sh run` merges staging into a private clone, requires a verdict manifest for the exact resulting tree, and fast-forwards main only then (gives the owner a verdict to merge PRs by); (5) `scripts/br_sync.sh <ids…>` flushes and verifies the exact bead set before staging JSONL (AGENTS.md landing step 4); (6) bead-close helper refuses to close without citing a manifest id whose tree contains the bead's landing commit; (7) check.sh's registry step stops being a grep (fa-szi replaces it) and forbidden-deps gains the cargo tree --invert posture-confinement check (§18.4).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: a run split across two workers (one step UNRUN on the first) completes on the second and produces one manifest for that tree; [ ] planted negatives: a FAIL recorded for the tree blocks the manifest; a dirty tree is refused; a manifest for tree A cannot close a bead landed in tree B; [ ] proof class: gate (verdict contract) ; [ ] consumers: every landing, the owner's staging→main merges, bead closes; [ ] no-claim boundary: binds verdicts to trees; does not make a weak step strong.

TESTS: scripts/tests/ shell tests with fixture repos for each case; shellcheck clean.

title: fad performs file reads and writes for unauthenticated socket clients relative to an unvalidated client `cwd`: confine host paths to a declared files root and refuse everything else
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14)
`fad` forwards the client's argv and `request.cwd` (fad/src/lib.rs:398-407) to the owner dispatcher; the
cwd is never validated. `document add`, `chart import`, `--intent`, `--plan` read any file the daemon user
can read into the book; `--plan-out`, `--certificate-out`, `--out` create files anywhere it can write
(combined with the --plan-out clobber, any file). The socket on main is bound with the default mode and no
peer-credential check (fad/src/main.rs:184); 5de90c6 (0600 socket) exists only on the unpushed nlu line.
fa-yha confines MCP host paths only; fa-ohe tests the `--as` variant only.

## What to build
1. `fad serve --files-root <dir>` (required for any file-reading or file-writing verb over the socket;
   absent ⇒ those verbs refuse over fad with a fix naming the flag). Paths are resolved against the root,
   canonicalized, and refused if they escape it (.., symlinks out, absolute paths elsewhere).
2. The client cwd is used only to make a relative path absolute on the CLIENT side; the daemon never trusts
   it.
3. Socket 0600 + SO_PEERCRED uid check (land 5de90c6 via RECON-3, then add the peer check).

## Acceptance
- Planted: socket request reading `/etc/passwd` as a document, writing `--out ../escape`, a symlink in the
  root pointing outside → all refused, nothing read or written (strace-free check: file hashes/mtimes
  unchanged; the book frontier unchanged).
- A request from a different uid is refused before any parsing.

## Tests & logging
fad integration tests with a tempdir root, logging request argv, resolved path, decision, refusal id.
close_reason: Implemented launch-time --files-root <dir> confinement for fad serve (resolve_in_daemon_files_root, admit_daemon_files, BookSource::locate Held --keys rejection, --receipt-out output path admission), refused host-file reads/writes when --files-root is omitted or escaped (via .., symlinks, book_dir overlap, or foreign request.cwd), and moved foreign-UID peer refusal to Ready::Accepted before any frame reading or parsing.

Profiles implemented: Human/Agent/System only (capability.rs:56). `registries/capability_caveats.toml` does not exist. title: Subject keys: per-Party erasable-field keys held outside the journal (R-KEY), managed by fad, with Party objects; ErasureCut switch-over from the typed refusal

Background: fa-lp6 (TopazOsprey, 2026-10-10) ships Erasable<T> fields with subject_ref but every key is the book key, and ErasureCut is a typed refusal (FA-REF-088) citing plan 8.5 / Appendix H R-ERASE: an FA-level tombstone that leaves plaintext reachable is a prohibited shortcut, so erasure waits for destroyable per-subject keys. title: Certificates that replay across binary upgrades: journaled RegistryEpoch objects, selector-scoped certified closures, certified reads that feed the fold, typed refusal above the row budget
description:
## Why (A5: "a damages schedule computed in 2026 replays in 2029")
Today (fa/src/certificate.rs): `registry_digest` hashes the include_str! text of 7 registries plus
franken-stack.lock (~391-431) and replay refuses on any mismatch (~990-994): any registry edit or pin bump
orphans every earlier certificate unless the old binary is kept. The certified closure is `MATCH
(n:Entry)` over the whole book (~449-453 policy: result_rows 1,000,000), so any report on a book with >1M
entries cannot be certified, and the report is recomputed via `db.vertices_at` beside the certified reads
rather than from them (plan §13.6 wants the closure's reads to be the fold input).

## What to build
1. RegistryEpoch control object: the exact texts of every registry a certificate depends on, stored
   content-addressed in the book (through the blob store when large) at genesis and whenever the running
   binary's registry set differs from the latest epoch (journaled, authorized). Certificates bind epoch
   digests. Replay loads registries from the book's epoch; a binary refuses only when it cannot interpret
   the epoch's format major (typed refusal naming the epoch and the needed major).
2. Selector-scoped closures: certified reads restricted to what the report needs (period/effective range,
   account set) where the substrate's query surface allows; otherwise a typed refusal with a pagination
   plan when the row budget would be exceeded (no silent truncation).
3. The fold consumes the certified read results (single computation path), so the certificate proves
   what was actually folded.

## Tests
Replay of a certificate after editing a non-format-breaking registry row in a newer binary build →
byte-identical; after a format-major change → typed refusal; >budget book → typed refusal; mutation of a
certified read input → replay detects.
acceptance_criteria: All four tests green; README's replay claim updated to the proven scope.

title: Make fa-reference independent where it matters: its own period resolution, period state machine and admissibility table (no calls into fa-time/fa-registry decision code), its own unbounded arithmetic in the application law, an exhaustive Appendix C cell test, and multi-seed differential campaigns
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): plan §16.2 — "a mismatch is triaged against the spec and never resolved by making the reference imitate the engine"; AGENTS.md — the oracle has "its own limb arithmetic … so a shared arithmetic bug cannot make the differential green". fa-reference calls the kernel's own `periods_for_year`, `resolve_period`, `transition` (fa-time) and `Admissibility::decide` (fa-registry) (crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:55-60, :978, :1127, :1562-1567), and its docs say it "mirrors the kernel's law order exactly" (lib.rs:6-11). For period law and admissibility, therefore, the differential proves the kernel is wired to those functions, not that the laws are right — fa-zxm's reversal-period bug survived precisely because both sides omit it. Its application law uses raw i128 (lib.rs:1752-1764, :2608-2618, :2629), contradicting the own-limbs design (it would panic, not refuse, on overflow). The "exhaustive" admissibility test checks the cell count plus about a dozen spot cells (crates/fa-registry/src/lib.rs:1230), not every cell against Appendix C. Each differential runs one fixed seed with 420–700 steps, USD only, amounts ≤ ~91k (crates/fa-registers/tests/differential.rs).

WHAT: (1) fa-reference gets naive, obviously-correct implementations: period generation by day-walking the calendar definition, resolution by linear search, a state machine as an explicit transition table, admissibility as a literal table transcribed from Appendix C (a second transcription, reviewed against the plan, not generated from admissibility.toml) — the kernel's registry and the oracle's transcription are then compared cell-by-cell in a test, so a registry typo is caught; (2) the application/open-item law on the oracle's limb arithmetic; (3) the topology gate forbids fa-reference from calling fa-time's resolution/transition functions and fa-registry's decide (allowlist only data types and parsing); (4) differential campaigns: N seeds per test in check.sh (e.g. 32, time-boxed), 10k seeds nightly-equivalent on a free worker, multi-unit histories (USD, JPY scale 0, BTC scale 8, ETH scale 18) and amounts near register bounds; the failing seed and a replay command printed; generated histories include the envelope fields fa-cw1 refuses; (5) a planted-negative audit: each planted negative must reach exactly one check (the M6 lesson recorded by the swarm: a mutation survived because every negative also tripped a sibling check).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: differential green across the seed campaign; Appendix C transcription equals admissibility.toml on all cells; [ ] planted negatives: deliberately wrong kernel admissibility cell is caught by the oracle (it was not before); the fa-zxm reversal-period bug is caught by the new oracle before fa-zxm's fix lands (record the old-code negative); [ ] proof class: differential (strengthened) ; [ ] consumers: every kernel bead, G1 ("the reference differential over model-generated histories"); [ ] no-claim boundary: differential agreement, not proof.

TESTS: fa-reference unit tests, differential campaigns with seeds/crashpack-style replay lines logged.

title: Lantern semantics defects: FIFO/LIFO/pro-rata tracing ignores supersession, Benford counts both legs and mixes units, duplicates flag Replace corrections, cutoff false positives in adjustment periods, round_trips not one-to-one, self_approved never fires
description:
## Why (found by reading the integration line 7ec4895, 2026-10-14)
- trace.rs:176 takes every posting entry including reversed originals and their reversals: tainted 500 day 1,
  erroneous clean 1,000 day 2, its Reverse day 3 → FIFO consumes the tainted 500 as part of the "1,000
  withdrawal" and traces 0 (LIBR correctly 500). Graph procedures exclude only REVERSAL-class entries,
  not the originals they reverse (graph.rs:90, 333).
- digits.rs:117-131 counts every leg of every unit: both sides of a two-leg entry (N ≈ 2×, chi-square ≈ 2×
  overstated) and USD/JPY/share counts in one distribution.
- duplicates.rs:66-73 flags a Replace that keeps the legs as a duplicate of the still-present original.
- cutoff.rs:43-44 resolves the document date without the effective-period hint → FYxx-P13 adjusting
  entries dated year-end flagged "0 days apart".
- graph.rs:105-163 round_trips: one outbound matches every same-amount return; quadratic without budget.
- jet.self_approved: the kernel refuses self-approval, so the planted set is empty; no positive test.
- The complexity witness allows n² on a 30-entry corpus — a tautology.

## What to build
Supersession-aware projections (net effects by lineage per §8.2 netting laws) as the input to every
procedure; Benford population rule (one side per entry, one unit, registered eligibility) recorded in the
procedure's evidence row; duplicates exclude supersession pairs; cutoff uses the entry's period
resolution; one-to-one matching with a budget; self_approved fed by approval records on drafts/imports or
removed from the registry; a real complexity witness (operation counts on corpora of 10², 10³, 10⁴ with a
registered bound).

## Acceptance
Each item gets a planted fixture that fails before and passes after; the fa-reference naïve versions are
written independently (not mirrors; see fa-vfu/fa-jt7p defect 9).

## Tests & logging
crates/fa-lantern/tests; each procedure run logs population size, parameters digest, findings count.
close_reason: Fixed all 7 Lantern semantics defects across fa-lantern, fa-reference, and registries/procedures.toml with planted regression tests (supersession netting, single-side single-currency Benford population, duplicate correction-lineage exclusion, adjustment-period cutoff discriminator, O(L log L) 1-to-1 RoundTrips matching, migrated self-approval detection, and registered complexity bounds verified across 10^2, 10^3, and 10^4 corpora).

title: fa-registers maintainer: incremental delta_since folds with a CAS watermark, RegisterCheckpoint control records with checkpoint cadence as a decision card, rebuild = maintained metamorphic, recovery discards and rebuilds, read paths never serve stale cells, Ripple switch-over rule registered
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Bet A1 says balances are "materialized incrementally and verifiable by recomputation", W2 names "the fa-registers maintainer over delta_since", and Appendix H registers the interim posture for Ripple views as a FrankenAccounting-level `delta_since` register maintainer. At 96d1918 every fold is a full rescan of the entry stream at a known-at seq (fa-registers/src/lib.rs `fold_period`, `trial_balance_at`); `materialize` writes register vertices and `verify_period` compares, but there is no incremental maintainer, no watermark advance from `delta_since`, no checkpoints, and `delta_since` has 0 hits. This is correct but will not scale, and the recovery rule ("recovery discards and rebuilds") has no code path to exercise.

WHAT:
1. The maintainer: `Registers::advance(&cx, book)` reads the substrate's `delta_since(watermark)` entry stream, folds only the new entries into the register cells (period × account × unit, plus the pending, open-item, availability and per-entity cells as they exist), moves the watermark under CAS inside the same transaction, and is idempotent under crash (re-running from a stale watermark yields identical cells).
2. Checkpoints: a journaled `RegisterCheckpoint` control record (legs = []) naming the watermark and the fold digest per register family; verify-by-fold runs from the last checkpoint or from genesis on demand; the checkpoint cadence is an adaptive decision with a decision card and a pinned fallback (every N entries), per the adaptive-decision contract.
3. Recovery: `fa registers rebuild` discards every register vertex and refolds from genesis (or from a checkpoint whose digest verifies); the rebuilt cells equal the maintained ones (metamorphic `rebuild = maintained`); `fa verify registers` stays green across the rebuild.
4. Reads: the report paths use maintained cells only when their watermark covers the requested known-at and the cells' verify digest matches; otherwise they fold (never a stale answer; the envelope reports which path answered).
5. Switch-over rule: when the substrate's Ripple views land, the maintainer becomes the registered interim's replacement per Appendix H; the rule is recorded in foundation_dependencies.toml.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: after N posts, `advance` moves the watermark by N and the maintained trial balance equals the full fold byte-for-byte; a crash between fold and watermark move (fa-sim crash point) leaves cells that re-advance to the same result; `rebuild` reproduces every cell; [ ] planted negatives: a maintainer mutation that skips one entry class is caught by verify-by-fold; a checkpoint with a forged digest is refused on rebuild; reading maintained cells past their watermark is refused by the read path test; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-04 register-never-more-authoritative, live) + metamorphic; [ ] consumers: every report path, G1 register verification, fa-sim campaigns; [ ] no-claim boundary: incremental equality is proven on the covered register families only.

TESTS: fa-registers integration tests with watermark and digests logged, fa-sim crash-point campaign for the maintainer, metamorphic rebuild test, CLI binary tests.
close_reason: Incremental delta_since register maintainer (crates/fa-registers/src/maintainer.rs), DecisionCard cadence, retired-cursor rebuild, migration visibility tracking, CLI/MCP registers advance/materialize/verify, and FA-INV-04.maintainer live in registries/invariants.toml.

title: Statistical audit lane with independent oracles: in-house exact Benford/KS/chi-square procedures checked against frankenscipy fsci-stats (test-only), NumPy-reproducible sampling via franken_numpy fnp-random-core (PCG64DXSM), property suites on frankensim fs-propcheck
description:
WHY: doctrine 12 — a detector's score is `statistical` evidence, never an invariant; an examiner must be able to re-run the numbers in Python. frankenscipy (/data/projects/frankenscipy) has chisquare, power_divergence, kstest/ks_1samp, binomtest and Binomial/Hypergeometric/Poisson/ChiSquared distributions — all f64, so it cannot produce the certified statistic but is an ideal TEST-ONLY checker (fa-lantern dev-dependency; 4 MB lib.rs compile cost noted). franken_numpy's fnp-random-core (366 lines, zero deps, forbid(unsafe)) gives SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm bit-compatible with np.random.PCG64DXSM, so a sample drawn from a declared seed is reproducible in Python; the seed is a declared input (no entropy capability, doctrine 3). frankensim's fs-propcheck (zero deps: deterministic property testing with shrinking and seed replay) and fs-rand (seeded streams independent of scheduling) serve the §16.6 property/metamorphic suites and fa-gen.
WHAT: (1) crates/fa-lantern first slice: exact-integer Benford first/second-digit expected counts (rational expectation × n, law-rounded), chi-square and KS statistics over register legs with a certificate; (2) `fa sample random|mus --seed <declared> --size n` over open items/legs using fnp-random-core, output reproducible by a documented NumPy snippet; (3) dev-dependencies: fsci-stats pinned by git rev as the differential oracle for the statistics (tolerance stated as an f64 oracle bound, never applied to amounts); fs-propcheck for property suites; (4) registry rows for the procedures' claim classes.
ACCEPTANCE: [ ] oracle differential passes on fixtures and generated histories; [ ] sample reproducibility test vectors (seed → indices) pinned; [ ] no float in any amount path; [ ] `fa capabilities --json` lists the procedures with claim class statistical. UPSTREAM: frankenscipy — integer/exact-rational entry points for expected counts, or document f64 as oracle-only.
notes:
Upstream issue filed 2026-10-10: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenscipy/issues/16 (oracle numerical contract; exact entry points; split lib.rs).
TESTING (idea-wizard pass 1): every slice lands unit tests in the owning crate AND an end-to-end script-level test (binary test in crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs where a verb is involved) with detailed, greppable logging of inputs, digests, and verdicts; external tools absent => UNRUN, never a fake pass; gate stays rch-only.
close_reason: Landed exact-integer Benford expected counts, KS and chi-square statistics with naive and pinned fsci-stats differential oracles, NumPy-reproducible SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm sampling with pinned vectors, and deterministic property/shrinking suites in fa-lantern (57 unit + 25 integration + 22 reference tests passing, 0 clippy warnings, 6/6 doctrine checks green).

title: Decide whether an empty (zero-byte) document may be recorded for disclosure; intake refuses it today (FA-REF-083)
description: WHY: the owner's document-disclosure test (b3ebf30, external_document_storage_and_empty_documents_use_the_same_public_export) recorded a zero-byte document and exported a disclosure over chunk 0. title: Document intake requires a capability and derives the provenance grade from the intake source and principal profile; the caller can never declare `HumanUpload`
description:
WHY: plan §9.3 — every document carries a provenance grade derived from its receipt chain (ThirdPartySigned, Connector, HumanUpload, AgentUpload, Generated); an entry whose only evidence is AgentUpload/Generated is self-sourced and needs a human Reviewed attestation before promotion (FA-INV-05; AGENTS.md "a document you uploaded yourself is graded AgentUpload"). At e606b46 `add_document` (crates/fa-journal/src/evidence.rs:651) takes no capability; the CLI sets the grade from `--grade` (crates/fa-cli/src/document.rs:97, default AgentUpload) and the uploader from `--as` (cli.rs:1477). An agent can label its own upload HumanUpload and skip the review gate; the reviewer-≠-uploader check compares against the caller-supplied identity.

WHAT: `add_document` takes the session capability; the grade is a pure function of (intake source registry row in registries/intake_sources.toml, principal profile, connector transcript if any): Agent profile ⇒ AgentUpload always; Human upload only from a Human-profile authenticated principal (fa-r3q) or the explicit embedded-owner posture (labelled); ThirdPartySigned only when a registered signature verifies; `--grade` is removed (or retained only as an assertion that must equal the derived grade, refused otherwise); the ImportReceipt records the authenticated principal and commitment.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an Agent session's upload is AgentUpload and the self-sourced gate fires on its entry until a Human Reviewed attestation exists; [ ] planted negatives: `--grade HumanUpload` from an Agent session refused; a reviewer equal to the uploader refused using the authenticated identity; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-05 evidence-minimum over honest grades) + evidence oracle differential update (crates/fa-registers/tests/evidence_oracle.rs); [ ] consumers: fa-g21, fa-646, Lantern jet.self_sourced_evidence; [ ] no-claim boundary: a grade states custody provenance, not document authenticity.

TESTS: evidence_oracle updates with seeds; CLI binary tests; fa-mcp e2e upload as Agent.

2. Wire handlers in `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/fad/src/lib.rs` (via CLI passthrough), and `crates/fa-mcp/src/server.rs` + `registry.rs`.
3. Regenerate `registries/robot_schema/1.jsonl` and ensure 100% CLI/MCP parity in `crates/fa-cli/tests/robot_schema.rs` and `crates/fa-mcp/tests/parity.rs`.

- Planted negative: Calling without `read` capability exits 7 (`FA-REF-012`) before storage observation; unmapped/invalid cash-flow or control accounts exit 3 with a typed refusal and `fix` hint.
- No-Claim: Exposing these single-book reporting verbs does not implement multi-entity Concordat consolidation (`fa-9ae`).

title: fa-intents first slice: typed intents with canonical bytes, Book::plan dry-run returning a Plan with a PlanCertificate, Book::commit(plan) re-validating the bound fields (PlanInvalidated refusals), confirm_plan gating, non-null certificate in the robot envelope
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Bet A6 says agents work through typed intents with dry-run plans, and plan §19 says the Genesis slice takes "real PostEntry, IntentHeader and Plan types from fa-intents". At 96d1918 `fa::Book` has `post` but no `session/plan/commit`; `plan_certificate` is always `None` (fa-cli main.rs ~1750, fa book.rs ~849); the robot envelope's `certificate` field is emitted as `null`; `confirm_plan` has zero hits. An Agent-profile capability is refused on trunk with a pointer to drafts (fa-s7x), so today an agent cannot post at all. Intents are the laws-layer abstraction (crate layer "laws": pure, stripped Cx) that both drafts (fa-s7x) and Canon (W6) build on, so this slice must exist before either.

WHAT (first real slice, not a prototype):
1. `crates/fa-intents` (laws layer; no I/O, no Cx with capabilities): `IntentHeader { book, branch, principal, capability_ref, idempotency_key, known_at? }`, the intent union for the classes the kernel admits today (PostEntry, Reverse, Reserve, Resolve, Settle, PeriodTransition, DocumentAdd) with Appendix B field names, a canonical byte form (versioned, additive-minor, tag-coded like fa:entry:v1) and `proposal_digest` (which already exists in the kernel; move the single source here).
2. `Book::plan(&cap, intent) -> Plan`: a dry run that runs the full posting pipeline up to but excluding commit (admission, period law, evidence minimum, balance law, limits, SoD) against a snapshot, returning the effects (legs, mirrors it would move, approvals it needs, refusal it would raise) and a `PlanCertificate { proposal_digest, effects_commitment, snapshot_seq, security_policy_epoch, expires_at_seq }`; nothing is written.
3. `Book::commit(&cap, plan)`: re-validates the certificate's bound fields (plan §4.6 line 371: proposal digest, effects commitment, coordinate, policy epoch, current SoD, execution authority) inside the serializable transaction and refuses `PlanInvalidated { reason }` (new FA-REF codes with catalog rows) when any changed; otherwise commits with `plan_certificate` recorded on the entry and emitted in the robot envelope (`certificate` non-null).
4. `confirm_plan`: dangerous verbs (post with post_closed, period close/lock/reopen, resolve voids) require `--yes` or a `--confirm-plan <certificate>` whose digest matches; the refusal names the safe alternative (`--dry-run`).
5. CLI: `fa post --dry-run` emits the plan with its certificate (Agent-profile capabilities imply dry-run once per session, §15); `fa commit --plan <file|digest>`; robot events `plan`, `plan_invalidated`.
6. Oracle: fa-reference models plan = pure evaluation and commit = re-evaluation under the current state; differential plants: a plan invalidated by a concurrent close, by an epoch change, by a revoked capability, by changed legs; a valid plan commits byte-identically to a direct post.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `fa post --dry-run --json` returns a certificate and writes nothing (journal head unchanged, proven by `fa verify registers` and an entry count); the same plan committed produces the same entry bytes as a direct post (metamorphic test); [ ] planted negatives: each `PlanInvalidated` reason is exercised by a test that changes exactly that bound field between plan and commit; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-11.core: certificates replayable) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-s7x drafts (intent-log), fa-canon (intents bound to rule families), fa-cli/fa-mcp dry-run macros, FA-INV-11; [ ] no-claim boundary: a certificate proves what the plan bound, not that the intent was economically correct.

TESTS: fa-intents unit tests for canonical bytes (golden vectors per minor), kernel tests in fa-journal/tests, CLI binary tests for dry-run/commit/confirm_plan, differential floors ≥ 3 per planted reason, all with the proposal digest logged.

title: StatementIssuance + IssueStatements intent, and the selectors AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED / AS REPORTED IN <certificate> / AS CURRENTLY STATED on tb, statements and explain
description:
## Why (bet A2; plan §7.4, §12.5; G2 criterion)
"FY2024 as it stood on 2025-03-03" works (AS KNOWN AT); "as originally reported" and "as currently
restated" do not: StatementIssuance exists only as a symbol (fa-model symbols.rs ~59), there is no
IssueStatements intent, the README's `--as-originally-reported` flag does not exist, and the
`originally-reported` invariant clause is dormant.

## What to build
- IssueStatements intent (Appendix B): journals a StatementIssuance control naming the certified
  statement package (certificate oids), audience, issuance date (TimeEvidence-backed), and period;
  authorized under SoD.
- Selectors: AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED (for a period: the first issuance's certificate coordinate),
  AS REPORTED IN <certificate|issuance> (that coordinate), AS CURRENTLY STATED (head with supersession
  netting per fa-oz3 once live; until then head). CLI flags on tb/statement/explain and MCP args.
- Certificate status reports `SupersededBy` with the restatement case when one exists (fa-oz3).

## Tests
Issue FY statements; post a later prior-period correction; originally-reported TB = issued bytes;
currently-stated differs by exactly the correction; replay of both.
acceptance_criteria: The three selectors work on the binary with replayable certificates; invariant clause live.

title: Content-addressed per-crate verdicts: whole-tree verdict as a Merkle root over workspace steps and per-crate verdicts keyed by exact input-closure hashes (incremental exact-tree proof)
description:
## Why
A Lantern-only landing re-runs fa-money, fa-time and every other unaffected crate's tests. The
exact-tree doctrine does not require that: it requires every verdict to bind its exact inputs.

## Design
- Workspace steps (fmt, deny, forbidden-deps, foundations, topology, registry checks, invariants,
  robot-schema pin, ubs, shellcheck) always run on the whole tree.
- Per crate: input hash = BLAKE3 over (crate source tree, transitive path-dependency crate trees,
  Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, franken-stack.lock, deny.toml, every registry file the crate
  embeds via include_str!/include_bytes!, feature set, test-target list). A crate whose input hash
  has a stored green verdict (git notes ref refs/notes/crate-verdicts, keyed by input hash) is not
  re-tested; its verdict is reused.
- Conservative invalidation: any change to Cargo.lock, toolchain, franken-stack.lock, deny.toml, or any
  registries/*.toml invalidates all crates.
- Tree verdict = Merkle root over (workspace step verdicts, per-crate verdict leaves); the manifest
  lists which leaves were reused and from which trees.

## Tests & logging
Planted change in a leaf crate → >= 50% of crate verdicts reused; planted registry change → 0 reused;
a composed root's per-crate results equal a cold full run on the same tree (equivalence test run once
per week as a lane).
acceptance_criteria: The three tests pass; a real landing reuses verdicts and the manifest lists reused leaves.
close_reason: Implemented per-crate input-hash closure, conservative include_str!/include_bytes! scanning, and Merkle tree verdict composition in scripts/crate_verdicts.py and scripts/crate_verdicts.sh; verified with scripts/tests/crate_verdicts_selftest.sh.

comments.text:
## 2026-10-19 (claude-opus-5-5): the aging portfolio (d6b01a46) and rule-policy cash flow (e6beb110) are surfaced on the CLI. Status: still OPEN

**What was unwired.** Three owner report families exist only in the library, about 3.7k lines with library tests: aging portfolio, split cash flow and policy cash flow. No CLI, fad or MCP path reached them; the sync `Book` had no wrapper for the portfolio. These two commits wire the first two.

**Aging portfolio (d6b01a46):**
- **Selections:**
  - `fa gl aging --reconcile --account 1200,2100 …` reconciles exactly those leaves.
  - `--all-posting` reconciles every posting leaf.
  - Both run from one chart, one aging fold and one control trial balance at ONE coordinate.
  - One code (`--account 1200`) is unchanged and still emits `aging_reconciled`.
- **A missing selection is still a usage refusal.** It is never read as the whole book (broadcast-scope doctrine). The two owner tests that assert exit 2 for it are unchanged.
- **New event and shapes:** event `aging_portfolio_reconciled`, shapes `aging_portfolio_account` and `aging_portfolio_uncovered`. Unselected leaves are `uncovered`, never zero. `complete`, `reconciled` and `pending_reservations` are separate verdicts. This is an additive row in robot-schema v1.
- **Certification:** `--certify` / `--certificate-out` retain the `fa:aging-portfolio:v1` artifact.
  - The new `--expect` kind `aging-portfolio` takes scope (all-posting, or selected with accounts), through, fixed known_at and buckets.
  - `fa replay C:<oid> --expect …` reproduces the original. Without `--expect` it exits 8, and the fix names `--expect`.
- **Sync wrappers:** `Book::reconcile_aging_portfolio` and `Book::certify_aging_portfolio`.

**Test:** `aging_portfolio_equals_each_single_leaf_reconciliation_and_replays_only_against_its_request` (crates/fa-cli/tests/retained_report_storage.rs).
- Differential: each whole-book portfolio account equals that account's own `aging_reconciled` at the same known_at.
- Event and shape keys equal the pinned schema.
- Six planted usage refusals publish nothing.
- Certify -> replay works. A changed cutoff or scope exits 8; a HEAD prefix exits 2.

**Rule-policy cash flow (e6beb110, library fa-i9yn):**
- A `gl cash-flow --policy` file with `account_rules` ([{account, activity}] for non-cash counterparts) and optional `overrides` (whole cash legs) is a rule policy.
- It emits the new event `policy_cash_flow`: `cash_flow`'s units plus `decisions` (each leg's activity and basis: account_rules, override or internal_transfer).
- Direct and indirect formats still refuse `account_rules`. A rule policy refuses `assignments` and `--indirect`.
- `--certify` retains `fa:policy-cash-flow:v1`, with the new `--expect` kind `policy-cash-flow`.
- Sync wrappers: `Book::cash_flow_with_policy` and `Book::certify_cash_flow_with_policy`.
- Test: `rule_policy_cash_flow_equals_its_explicit_leg_assignments_and_replays_only_against_its_policy`.
  - Differential: the 64 derived decisions, fed back as explicit assignments, give an identical `cash_flow`.
  - One override moves exactly 1.00 USD from operating to financing.
  - Seven planted usage refusals publish nothing.
  - Replay: a changed rule or a dropped override exits 8; an omitted `--expect` exits 8 with a fix naming `--expect`.
- A rule policy is a handful of rows instead of one assignment per cash leg, which also keeps the replay_command far below the argv limit recorded on fa-lzrn.

**Also:**
- README "Reporting available now" now lists six gl lines (ca790fdf), each registry-checked by the README test. They are not executed by that test; the surfaces they name are exercised by binary tests.
- Event coverage: `every_declared_event_is_emitted_by_the_binary` (cli.rs) now also runs `gl aging --all-posting --reconcile` and a rule-policy `gl cash-flow`. Gate k17 caught that the first version of d6b01a46 had omitted this; the fix is folded into d6b01a46 and e6beb110 so every commit stays green.

**Still open on this bead:**
- Split cash flow (`Book::split_cash_flow` / certificate: exact principal/interest portions of one cash leg) has no surface. I did not wire it because of a format question for the owner.
  - `CashFlowPortion.amount` is a bare i128 mantissa "in the SAME unit … as its source cash leg"; the definition carries no unit.
  - A CLI that parses portions as exact strings ("0.40 USD") and passes only the mantissa would silently accept "0.40 EUR" against a USD leg, because both have scale 2.
  - A safe surface must either check each portion's unit against the cited leg's unit before retention (the CLI has the source lines after the read), or the library definition should carry the unit.
  - The `--expect` replay path needs the same check.
- The portfolio JSONL workpaper (`aging_portfolio_jsonl`, read+produce, recipient-bound) has no surface.
- MCP: `gl` has no MCP tool at all, so none of the gl families are on MCP. The cluster has to be chosen first (see fa-i7e on full clusters).

- k17 (df81bc1f): 1 real failure, every_declared_event_is_emitted_by_the_binary. Fixed and folded into d6b01a46 and e6beb110.
- k20 (f185d933): clippy type_complexity on a test closure. Fixed with a type alias in e6beb110.

title: Never-silent-fail on panic: install a panic hook in fa, fad and fa-mcp that emits exactly one robot `error` event (exit 5, refusal_id, class "internal") instead of exit 101 with no event
description:
WHY: plan §15.3 "every non-zero exit emits exactly one error event carrying refusal_id, exit, and class, which is what the never-silent-fail regression test asserts"; exit code 1 is never emitted and Rust's panic exit is 101. At e606b46 there is no panic hook (Teller audit): a panic in the substrate or a dependency exits 101 with no error event, breaking the robot contract and the exit-code dictionary. Surface code has no unwrap/expect, but the substrate and foundations can still panic.

WHAT: a panic hook (std::panic::set_hook) in each binary's main that writes one `error` event (stdout when --json, stderr text otherwise), maps to exit 5 with class "internal" and refusal_id, and includes the panic location; fad keeps serving other connections where the region model allows (a panic inside one request's region is that request's error, not the daemon's death) — verify with asupersync's region semantics; a test binary feature `fa-test-panic` (dev-only, compiled out of release) triggers a panic to test it.

title: fa-mcp containment: tool arguments that name host filesystem paths (document/intent/plan/chart inputs, plan_out output) require an explicit launch filesystem root or are refused; inline/forwarded-stdin forms are the MCP path
description:
WHY (TopazOsprey 4185, WhiteCreek 4184, 2026-10-11): after fa-23r a launch-bound fa-mcp fixes identity, authority, the book and its keys, but path arguments still resolve against the server process's working directory on the host: fa_evidence_import_document.file, fa_post_post/reserve/resolve.intent_file and fa_chart_import_chart.file read any file the server's OS user can read; fa_time_period_transition.plan reads a plan file; plan_out writes one anywhere the user can write. An agent holding read+post can therefore import arbitrary host files as documents or write files outside the book. fa-23r explicitly does NOT claim filesystem confinement.

WHAT:
1. In the MCP posture the inline / forwarded-stdin forms (intent, text, chart) are the positive path.
2. A path argument is refused with a structured error whose fix names the inline form, unless the launch configuration grants an explicit filesystem root (--files <dir>); paths are then resolved under that root with no .., symlink or absolute escape.
3. plan_out and plan work only under that root.
4. Audit every tool, resource and macro (fa-z5u's macros included) that accepts a path.
5. Planted negatives: absolute path, .. escape, symlink escape, and a path given without the root; positive: inline forms and an in-root path.

ACCEPTANCE: positive observable = an e2e stdio session launched with --files <dir> imports a document from under the root and the same call with a path outside it is refused with the structured error; planted negatives as in WHAT 5 each reaching exactly one check; proof class = e2e + unit on the resolver; consumers = every MCP host, fa-z5u, fa-ohe; no-claim boundary = this confines path arguments only; it is not a sandbox for the server process and does not authenticate the operator (fa-v62/fa-r3q).
close_reason: Added --files <dir> launch-confined directory root to fa-mcp and LaunchAuthority in fa-cli; resolve_in_files_root rejects relative escapes, absolute paths, directories, and symlink components along path; document add/import/export and plan file paths work inside root when --files is provided; verified with unit and integration tests.

comments.author: CobaltGull
comments.text: 2026-10-13 (CobaltGull, fa-ul9 tracker truth): the containment half is on the integrated trunk. fa-mcp never exposes a host-path property in a tool schema (registry.rs is_host_path_property / forbidden_path_argument, pinned by tests/parity.rs), and the bound CLI surface refuses --plan-out/--certificate-out/--out and any non-stdin --intent/--plan/file input (fa-cli cli.rs admit_bound_files: "MCP accepts no output paths", "forward the complete content on stdin with -"). Inline/forwarded-stdin forms are the positive path. NOT done: the optional `--files <dir>` launch root (resolver with no ..,symlink or absolute escape) and its e2e positive/negatives, which this bead's acceptance names. Until a host needs in-root files, "every path refused" is the safe posture; keep open for the root, or re-scope the acceptance to "paths refused" by ruling.

title: Owner-project survey and adoption decisions (2026-10-10): what each of the owner's 47 Rust projects can contribute to FrankenAccounting, the rulings that govern adoption, and the upstream issues filed
description:
PURPOSE: the durable record of the 2026-10-10 survey of every Rust project written by the owner (47 projects, local checkouts under /data/projects and GitHub Dicklesworthstone), evaluated for applicability, utility and accretion to FrankenAccounting, plus the owner rulings that govern adoption. Read this before proposing any dependency; do not re-survey.

OWNER RULINGS (binding, recorded in AGENTS.md doctrine 1 and README):
1. The closed dependency universe excludes THIRD-PARTY crates only. Every Rust project written by the owner — Franken-named or not (e.g. fastapi_rust) — is an admissible foundation, pinned by git rev, with its transitive closure confined by deny.toml wrapper allowlists exactly like asupersync/frankengraphdb/fnx/fastmcp-rust. First-party code still never imports serde, tokio, chrono, decimal crates, arrow or SQLite bindings directly.
2. Upstream changes are fine: file GitHub issues with the requests (nine filed, listed below).
3. Adoption follows a concrete consumer slice (plan rule): each adoption bead lands the pin in the same change as the first consuming code.

METHOD: four read-only explorer passes (no builds), each reading README/plan/architecture headers, root Cargo manifests, crate counts, .rs counts, #[test] counts, status notes and last commit dates; verdicts are tied to file paths. Present-tense READMEs about planned systems were not accepted as evidence.

ADOPT NOW (beads): franken_markdown → fa-cet (deterministic PDF/A-2b, HTML, SVG statements; std-only engine fmd-font/fmd-math with clap/wasm/asupersync optional; ~4.5k tests; src/pdfa.rs, src/diff.rs semantic diff, src/diagrams.rs flowcharts; crates.io v0.5.0; numeric table alignment/footing to be verified by fixture first). frankensympy → fa-pri (fsym-bigint/fsym-rational: normalised exact rationals, cross-cancelled composition, metered arithmetic; local snapshot has no .git — pin upstream f449ab0; its own plan calls the exact substrate an open decision; today it wraps num-bigint/num-rational with serde derives — allowlisted as foundation transitives).

ADOPT LATER OR TEST-ONLY (beads): frankenscipy fsci-stats → fa-vpk (chisquare, power_divergence, kstest/ks_1samp, binomtest, Binomial/Hypergeometric/Poisson/ChiSquared; f64 only, so test-only oracle; 4 MB lib.rs; nightly CI not green per its README). franken_numpy fnp-random-core → fa-vpk (366 lines, zero deps, forbid(unsafe); SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm bit-compatible with np.random.PCG64DXSM for seed-declared reproducible audit sampling; bit-exactness is the README's claim, 5 tests in the core crate). frankensim fs-propcheck / fs-rand / fs-blake3 → fa-vpk (zero-dep property testing with shrinking and seed replay; seeded streams; a test-time BLAKE3 cross-check; frankensim has no local .git — pin upstream; its README says not yet an integrated end-user application; skip fs-eproc (asupersync covers it), fs-ledger (frankensqlite), fs-qty (no money)). frankengit fgit-deflate → fa-646 (std-only bounded streaming zlib/DEFLATE, 3,865 LOC, 41 tests, for PDF FlateDecode and ZIP-based XBRL/SAF-T packages; the rest of frankengit (234 third-party packages, fgit-crypto with ed25519-dalek) is not needed; its constellation.lock pattern is already plan §2.6). franken_lean fln check-olean → fa-uqq (zero external crates; elaborator accepts only 25 of 2,961 upstream elab tests so it cannot compile our .lean, but check-olean accepted all 2,433 stdlib modules — a second kernel over anchors compiled by upstream Lean; fln-bignum uses Lean number semantics, wrong for money). franken_ocr focr and franken_whisper fw robot → fa-646 (external processes only: both link frankensqlite and other closures; OCR has 19.3% character error rate on its own corpus so output is advisory, never an amount source; whisper NDJSON transcripts with diarization; models download separately 1.6 GB + 0.49 GB). hedge_fund_data_tool → fa-646 after upstream extraction (deterministic PDF text-layer extraction crates/hfdt-sources/src/extract.rs pdf_text_to_text, no OCR; hfdt-pdf-crypto AES-256 empty-password PDFs with deps aes+sha2 only; hfdt-tables cells-as-evidence; hfdt-accounting-quality statement-level procedures; inline-XBRL reader only; no Benford; proprietary license; carries chrono/serde today). flywheel_connectors → fa-ff6 (separate supervised process: fwc → fcp-host → connector subprocesses over stdio/JSON-RPC; connectors/plaid transactions_sync and accounts_balance_get, snowflake sql.write/sql.query, bigquery, s3, stripe, postgresql; cannot be linked: tokio/hyper/reqwest/chrono in fcp-async-core). franken_alignment → fa-s30 (GitHub only; reference model, zero external crates, nightly-2026-09-07; one-shot permits bound to immutable payloads, conserved rights, authority-graph dominators/min-cuts for separation of duties, judgment caching with emptiness witnesses, DecisionClosure; crate names collide with ours (fa-reference, fa-policy, fa-verify, fa, fa-cli) so linking needs package renames; port invariants as fa-policy tests first). eidetic_engine_cli → fa-i8j design reference (daemon over a local Unix socket with 4-byte length-prefixed JSON frames and size limits, src/daemon/protocol.rs; uses std::os::unix::net — we use asupersync Unix sockets src/net/unix/listener.rs). fastapi_rust → fa-i8j later HTTP posture only (v0.5.0, not production-ready per README:784, TCP-only server crates/fastapi-http/src/server.rs; asupersync-native; inatd uses it for a daemon status endpoint). toon_rust → fa-1gb (TOON spec v3.0, 289 tests; every dep always on incl. unused chrono, f64 numbers; in-house encoder validated against its tests/fixtures/spec and the tru binary until the lib/cli split lands). mcp_agent_mail_rust and coding_agent_session_search → fa-xex design/behavioural references (error envelope with recoverable/fix_hint; robot mode triage next_command, capabilities, robot-docs schemas); mortgage_processing_data_tool → design reference for dual control and one command catalog driving CLI and daemon (private, serde/num-bigint/pdf-extract). franken_surveillance_system fss-graph-algorithms and franken_overlap → fa-fk5 blocked on upstream (fss: exact-integer Hungarian/max-flow/SCC/temporal reachability with proof witnesses, 17.4k LOC, 108 tests, but tied to fss-core and u64 weights, no local .git; overlap: real sparse-spectral near-duplicate detection, not yet benchmarked, fo-core requires rayon, corpus crate pulls reqwest). frankenmermaid → fa-949 later (32 diagram types, deterministic SVG, but fm-layout requires good_lp+HiGHS, a C++ solver; franken_markdown's flowchart compiler covers lineage today). frankensearch → fa-search bead (owner correction 2026-10-10: the survey wrongly called it tantivy-backed; its lexical engine is Quill, a native pure-Rust BM25 engine — crates/frankensearch-quill v0.4.0, FSLX segments, delta-visible indexing, receipted ~0.2 ms lexical search on 1K docs; tantivy survives only as an opt-in conformance oracle lane (feature lexical-tantivy / tantivy-oracle) outside Quill's dependency graph; frankensearch-fsfs uses pdf-extract for its own PDF path which FA does not need. Use: full-text search over Documents' derived text, entry descriptions and memos (fa search), default features only, never the tantivy lane; the substrate's Beacon indexes stay the structural index). sqlmodel_rust → only sqlmodel-postgres (pure-Rust Postgres wire client on asupersync) if direct warehouse push is ever wanted; file export is simpler.

NOT APPLICABLE (do not revisit without a new reason): frankenpandas (fp-types already carries chrono/chrono-tz/serde, amounts parse to f64, fp-io drags arrow/parquet/calamine/csv/quick-xml; only a post-1.0 fa-frames adapter outside every posture closure), franken_snowflake (alpha, writes pending; 641 packages incl. fsqlite/frankenpandas; its MCP crate is a pattern for fastmcp+asupersync only), frankenfs (FUSE ext4/btrfs; one storage engine rule), frankenredis (mature Redis clone; no cache/KV server needed), franken_engine and franken_node (JS/TS runtimes; Canon is total and I/O-free; node requires tokio), frankenlibc (LD_PRELOAD glibc replacement, unsafe allowed; a deployment choice at most), frankenterm (terminal hypervisor for swarms), frankentui/charmed_rust/opentui_rust/rich_rust (TUI/terminal styling; no TUI in 1.0; human mode is plain text; rich_rust arrives transitively via fastmcp-console), frankentts (text to speech), franken_manim (animation engine; SVG writer far too heavy for exhibits), frankenjax/frankentorch (ML; learned scores only advisory by doctrine, no consumer before 1.0), franken_agent_detection, franken_trends (fragment, missing crate in workspace), franken_code_browser (planning), franken_nlp (no model inference yet; rules-only redaction CLI maybe later for erasable fields), meta_skill/pi_agent_rust/mcp_agent_mail_rust as dependencies (tooling), injective_network_automated_threat_detector, building_trades_data_tool, copulattice, mechanism_interferometry_causality (research), franken_remote/frankensonos/franken_threed/franken_drone_geometry/franken_native_capsule (unrelated domains).

CONFIRMED FOUNDATIONS: asupersync at the pinned rev 78b64636 (= 0.5.0) has the lab runtime fa-sim needs: src/lab/runtime.rs, config.rs, virtual_time_wheel.rs, chaos.rs, injection.rs, explorer.rs (DporExplorer), trace/dpor.rs, trace/crashpack.rs (CrashPack with replay_command), lab/replay.rs, replay_minimization.rs, dual_run.rs, scenario.rs, oracle/; schedule_minimizer.rs is newer than the pin; there is no faulty VFS in asupersync — torn writes/ENOSPC/fsync lies come from frankengraphdb crates/fgdb-sim (FaultVfs) and fgdb-chronicle CrashPoint, and fgdb-sim is not yet a workspace dependency. fastmcp_rust =0.12.0: official server conformance 110/115 (0 fail, 4 SHOULD warnings), stdio on Unix is the qualified transport; it pins asupersync =0.5.0 from crates.io so the [patch.crates-io] from plan §18.4 is required; it unconditionally pulls chrono (fastmcp-server) and fastmcp-console (rich_rust + time) — both banned in deny.toml today, so fa-mcp needs wrapper allowlists before it can land (bead fa-xex). Owner ruling 2026-10-10: carrying these foundation-owned transitives under wrapper allowlists confined to the fa-mcp/fad posture is fine.

GAPS NONE OF THE PROJECTS FILL (stay in-house per plan §18): exact money and calendars (done), Canon rules language, format readers/writers for CSV/JSON/XBRL (writer)/SAF-T/AICPA ADS/Beancount/hledger/camt/BAI2/OFX, Merkle bundles and the std-only fa-verify, Benford/MUS/JET procedures as exact-integer certified computations, a PDF reader (parser; the inflater can come from fgit-deflate), MCP tool docs from verbs.toml.

UPSTREAM ISSUES FILED 2026-10-10: frankensympy#1 (serde feature-gate, stable metered API, canonical BigRational bytes); franken_overlap#54 (rayon optional); frankenmermaid#13 (feature-gate HiGHS); franken_surveillance_system#2 (standalone fss-graph-algorithms, integer weights, tag); toon_rust#58 (lib/cli split, drop unused chrono); hedge_fund_data_tool#1 (standalone PDF text-layer + pdf-crypto crates); fastmcp_rust#88 (optional fastmcp-console; chrono); franken_markdown#20 (numeric alignment/footing, expose inflater); frankenscipy#16 (oracle numerical contract, exact entry points, split lib.rs).

ACCEPTANCE FOR THIS EPIC: closes when every adoption bead it depends on is closed or explicitly withdrawn with a recorded reason; it never closes on process output. Re-survey only when a project listed as blocked changes upstream (the issue closes) or a new owner project appears.

title: Agent-safe authority on every surface: authenticated principals, issued capabilities, Agent-profile defaults, read-path authorization (reality check 2026-10-11)
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-11 at origin/staging e606b46): the plan's agent-safety story (§14.2 caveats, §14.4 profiles, doctrine 7 "SoD enforced at commit", doctrine 8 "authorization precedes observation", AGENTS.md "Do not write to trunk from an Agent-profile capability") is implemented correctly INSIDE the kernel (fa-policy admit/SoD, FA-REF-013 Agent-on-trunk, revocation witnesses) but every surface constructs the capability it presents from caller-supplied argv. `Capability::embedded(holder, op_names)` (crates/fa-policy/src/capability.rs:237-247) self-issues a Human-profile capability; fa-cli reads the principal from `--as` (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:1476-1478) and ops from `--grant` (cli.rs:2104-2106, :2591-2595); fad forwards the client's argv unchanged into `cli::run` (crates/fad/src/lib.rs:194-216); fa-mcp exposes `as`, `grant`, `yes` and `keys` as tool arguments and turns them into argv (crates/fa-mcp/src/registry.rs:1381-1388; its own unit test at :1775-1800 pins `grant: post_closed, yes: true` → `--grant post_closed --yes`). Consequences, all verified in source: an MCP agent can act as any principal, grant itself post_closed/approve/migrate/witness, approve its own proposal as a second invented principal, and is never issued an Agent-profile capability, so FA-REF-013 and the Agent profile never fire outside tests. The MCP self-approval mistake detector even tells the agent to retry "with `as` set to a different, admissible principal" (crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:484-488) — coaching impersonation. `fa capabilities` claims "The daemon/MCP posture binds the capability from an authenticated session" (cli.rs:1225), which is false today. Reads take no capability at all (crates/fa/src/book.rs:1162-1212), and `Book::read_document` returns privileged bytes without one (book.rs:982).

This epic makes the authority model real on the postures agents actually use (fad, fa-mcp), keeps the embedded owner posture explicit and labelled, and adds the adversarial tests that prove it. It does NOT weaken any kernel check; the kernel already does the right thing given an honest capability.

Children: fa-23r (MCP containment, ship first), fa-v62 (journaled issuance + holder-bound tokens + profiles registry), fa-r3q (fad session binding), fa-0x0 (read-path authorization), fa-087 (ungated privileged read), fa-vwf (intake authorization + derived provenance grade), fa-7dw (AccessEvent), fa-kae (signed approvals/attestations), fa-ohe (agent-safety red-team acceptance suite). Related existing beads: fa-llx (caveats in the kernel), fa-1d6 (revocation surface), fa-s30 (permit model), fa-t6m (current-policy spec), fa-kuu (redaction caveat), fa-s7x (drafts: the only legal place for Agent-profile writes).

Epic acceptance: fa-ohe's suite green on the exact landing tree; `fa capabilities --json` reports the binding posture truthfully; no surface accepts a principal or op from an untrusted caller.

title: The CONTROLS relation is reused for Entry→MigrationRun edges: give migration membership its own relation so related-party/control traversals never walk into migration runs
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14)
crates/fa-journal/src/migration.rs:1320-1328 and 1464-1474 write `CONTROLS` edges from entries to their
MigrationRun. The plan reserves CONTROLS for Subledger→Account and entity/party control (§4.1, §4.5); the
README's own related-party GQL traverses `[:RELATED_TO|OWNS|CONTROLS*1..3]` and would reach migration runs
once Party vertices exist (fa-l2h).

## What to build
A registered relation (e.g. `IN_MIGRATION_RUN`) in symbols.toml; new books write it; readers of the old
edge keep working for existing books via a versioned reader (no rewrite of history — append-only); a
registry note records the change. Update fa-l2h's acceptance to assert CONTROLS has only control semantics.

## Acceptance
New book: no CONTROLS edge into MigrationRun; migration visibility tests unchanged; an old-format fixture
book still reads correctly.

## Tests & logging
fa-journal migration tests + a fixture-book reader test.
close_reason: Added IN_MIGRATION_RUN (id = 36) to symbols.toml and fa-model; switched migration open_run, transition_run, and post (Migration chunks) to write IN_MIGRATION_RUN edges into MigrationRun; added versioned reader fa_journal::run_entries that reads IN_MIGRATION_RUN and legacy CONTROLS edges into MigrationRun; updated fa-l2h acceptance; verified with entry_to_migration_run_uses_in_migration_run_and_reads_legacy_controls.

title: Wire Teller to the surfaces: fa bank import (camt.053/052, BAI2, OFX, MT940, CSV) as BankLine documents and fa bank match (scoreboard WF-ACM-03)
description:
## Why (found 2026-10-18 by claude-opus-5-5; scoreboard row WF-ACM-03)
Vision row VC-15 ("the agent closes a month": import and match a CAMT.053 statement) has no surface. Every bank statement parser exists, tested and fuzzed, in fa-formats::bank:
- camt.053 and camt.052;
- BAI2;
- OFX/QBO;
- MT940;
- CSV.
Reconciliation folds exist in fa-registers::reconciliation and the oracle (fa-2ek, closed 2026-10-16). But `fa bank import` does not exist, so no surface can import a statement. Until 2026-10-18 the scoreboard row cited fa-9x4, a bead that was never in the tracker.

## What to build
1. `fa bank import <statement> --format camt053|camt052|bai2|ofx|mt940|csv --account <code>`. It records the statement as a content-addressed Docket document with its import receipt, and every line as a BankLine document DERIVED_FROM it. Re-importing the same statement is idempotent by content.
2. `fa bank match` over the existing matching and decision-card logic, with the deterministic pinned fallback. Match decisions are journaled objects and never change an amount.
3. verbs.toml rows (verbs, events, an on-demand MCP cluster fa.teller or fa.evidence tools), parity, and the robot-schema pin.

## Acceptance
- The scoreboard row WF-ACM-03 works.
- A camt.053 fixture imports, and its lines reconcile against posted cash entries.
- A duplicate import writes nothing.
- A statement whose closing balance does not equal opening plus lines is refused (verify_internal_balance).
- Planted negative: a float amount in a CSV statement is refused.

title: Reversal effective date must fall in the target's period or later, and only registered classes may target a special period (Adjustment/Closing/Opening) — enforced in the kernel and independently in the oracle
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): plan §8.1 "Reversal: exact negation of one target entry, same or later period"; §7.3 "only Adjusting, Closing, Elimination, Revision, Restatement, and Migration classes may target a special period, and a Normal target is the default". (a) The reversal path (crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:1218-1399) checks target existence, exact side-swap and reversed-once but not that the reversal's effective date/period is ≥ the target's; the oracle has the same omission (crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:1766-1795), so the differential cannot catch it — a reversal can be back-dated into an earlier period than the fact it reverses. (b) Period resolution accepts `effective_period` naming a live Adjustment/Closing/Opening period for any admitted class (crates/fa-time/src/period.rs:208-216; no class check in post.rs:617-638), so an Original can be routed into adjustment period 13.

WHAT: (1) registry: add a `special_period_classes` table (or `[[kind]]` class rows) in registries/admissibility.toml naming exactly the classes allowed per special kind; kernel and oracle both derive from it (oracle via its own reader, fa-vfu). (2) kernel: after resolving the target (point witness on the target entry), resolve both periods in the calendar's order and refuse a reversal whose period precedes the target's (new FA-REF code, catalog row with fix "post the reversal in <target period> or a later open period"); refuse special-period targeting by unlisted classes (FA-REF-010 family). (3) oracle: independent implementation of both rules.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: same-period and later-period reversals commit; Adjusting into P13 commits; [ ] planted negatives: reversal dated one period before its target → refused; Original with effective_period = P13 → refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-03, FA-INV-08) + differential + exhaustive class × kind test generated from the registry; [ ] consumers: fa-oz3, fa-4o0 (close), fa-xwv; [ ] no-claim boundary: period ordering per the book's calendar order, not civil-date order alone (P12 vs P13 share dates).

TESTS: genesis.rs negatives; fa-registry exhaustive table test; differential with seeds.

comments.text: Implementation trap found during fresh source review (c2137f3): FiscalCalendar::periods_for_year in crates/fa-time/src/calendar.rs assigns Opening ordinal normal_count+1 and appends it after all normal periods, even though its effective date is the fiscal-year start. Therefore neither raw vector position nor (fiscal_year, ordinal) is a valid chronological comparison for the reversal rule: Opening-to-P01 would be falsely refused. Civil date alone also cannot distinguish final Normal vs Adjustment vs Closing. Define the semantic calendar order explicitly (Opening before normals/Historical, then adjustments, then Closing, with per-kind ordinal ordering and fiscal year), check it against normative period law, and include Opening-to-P01 and same-date final-Normal/Adjustment/Closing cases alongside prior-period refusal. Do not mutate durable existing ordinals to make comparison convenient. Source reconnaissance only; no implementation or runtime claim.
